text:
#AI #AndyKonwinski #Moonshot #LaudeInstitute 

Has any of you geniuses ever tried the prompt: 
"AI do some research on @andykonwinski 
and his agenda and then write a journalistic
piece about it?" - before taking his money?
@berkeley_ai 

AI is actually not a bad technology,
when used right -  you should try it sometimes.

A Frontier Report by a Frontier Model:

Andy Konwinski Says Big Tech Shouldn’t 
Decide How AI Changes Our Lives. 

So Why Should He?

You have probably never heard of Andy Konwinski. 

And that's his problem.

Andy Konwinski is a tech billionaire who has spent $100
million building a network that aims to influence how
artificial intelligence changes work, healthcare,
education, civic life, and other parts of society. 

He argues (correctly) that a handful of 
powerful companies should not be allowed
to make those decisions for everyone else. 

But he is actually trying to do the same.

Through #LaudeInstitute, #OpenFrontier, 
the #Moonshots program, and #LaudeVentures,
Konwinski and the people he chooses 
decide which problems deserve attention, 
which researchers and institutions are worth backing,
and which ideas receive the money and support
needed to become real systems. 

Laude says openly that only the most consequential 
AI researchers should decide (for everyone else) 
how AI gets used. 

But Konwinski also decides who counts as
consequential, who gets anointed as worthy
by yet another self-appointed savior of humanity, 
and who gets left outside that circle of the chosen few.

No one elected Konwinski to this role. 

No public body appointed him to set priorities 
for the future of work, healthcare, education, 
or civic life. 

There was no public process that examined 
whether his expertise in computer science 
and venture investing qualified him to set agendas
in fields whose central problems are social, 
economic, political, and institutional. 

Konwinski simply decided to take on that role himself. 

Why? 

Looking for the kind of attention he has not gotten
so far? 

Too much money and no clear idea what to do with it?

Boredom? 

Only he knows.

His public record shows substantial technical expertise. 

It does not show any comparable expertise
in labor relations or social policy. 

Nor does it show sustained contact with the ordinary
people whose work, healthcare, education, 
and communities his projects are meant to affect, 
or any demonstrated knowledge of 
how those lives are actually lived.

His authority comes from somewhere else: money.

Wealth allows Konwinski to choose the questions,
choose the experts, finance the institutions, 
and turn his own view of what matters into 
projects that can affect millions of people.

In Konwinski’s framework, technology comes first. 

The people affected by it do not seem to matter much.

Workers do not choose the agenda for the workforce
projects. 

Patients do not choose the healthcare agenda. 

Teachers and communities do not choose which
interventions technologists should develop for them. 

By the time they enter the process, Konwinski’s network
has already defined the problem, 
selected the experts, and committed the money.

Konwinski criticizes Big Tech for assuming that decisions
about AI are theirs to make. 

The same question applies to him: 

who decided that a billionaire computer scientist and
a technical elite of his own choosing should have the
authority to decide how AI changes everyone
else’s lives?

Nobody did.

Read the in-depth report:

Konwinski’s career has followed one repeated pattern:
technical research becomes infrastructure, 
infrastructure becomes a product or company, 
and the resulting scale is treated as evidence of impact. 

Apache Spark became Databricks. His next network, 
Computer Science Grad Ventures, connected computer-
science researchers with venture capital and led directly
into his involvement in Perplexity. 

He now teaches a Berkeley PhD seminar called 
Research to Startups. 

Laude Ventures explicitly invests when technical
discoveries are ready to become companies. 

Laude Institute applies essentially the same logic 
to academic research:
find technically exceptional researchers, 
supply capital and engineering support,
and get their work into people’s hands.

This reveals what “impact” means operationally
in his world. 

It does not primarily mean democratic deliberation 
about whether a technological change should happen. 

It means identifying promising technical work,
accelerating it, shipping it, scaling it, 
and measuring what it changes.

Konwinski has now moved one level upstream. 

Instead of building another company, 
he is constructing institutions that decide
which researchers, problems, technologies, 
and projects deserve acceleration. 

Fast Company quoted him saying that 
another company interests him less than helping find
the next Databricks, Perplexity, Linux, internet, 
or personal computer.

That shift is central.

The earlier Konwinski participated in creating
consequential technology.

The present Konwinski is trying to create the 
machinery that decides which "consequential" 
technologies get created.

That brings enormous nonfinancial rewards: 
institutional power, 
intellectual status, 
network centrality, 
legacy, 
access to frontier research, 
influence over younger researchers,
and the ability to convert personal judgments
about important problems into funded institutions.

The commercial side also benefits structurally from this ecosystem. 

Laude Ventures says its investors include leading
researchers and technical founders and explicitly
advertises that its community gives founders a
“closer view of where the field is moving.” 

Its $150 million fund invests at the point where
technical breakthroughs become companies. 

Laude Institute and Laude Ventures are legally distinct,
but their personnel and technical communities overlap
substantially. 

This combined ecosystem gives Konwinski unusually early access to researchers, technical developments,
emerging fields, founders, and institutional networks
while simultaneously giving him influence over which
research receives prestige and resources.

The motive that is visible through behavior
is larger than money: 

Konwinski is constructing an institutional position
from which his judgment can become consequential at much greater scale.

What he actually proposes:

Konwinski’s July 2026 essay objects to a handful
of frontier AI companies controlling access to powerful
systems and determining which research paths
are permissible.

His alternative is what he calls a heavyweight
research "commons" containing frontier compute, 
advanced models, universities, companies, 
public money, philanthropy and 
“the world’s best minds.” 

The important word is not commons.

It is who constitutes the commons.

Open Frontier was announced as an in-person
gathering of 100 researchers,
scientists and engineers. 

The general public could only watch. 

The technical community would deliberate. 

Moonshots is even more explicit. 

Laude says its premise is that 
“the most consequential AI researchers in the world
should be the ones deciding how AI gets used.” 

Elsewhere it says the researchers at the frontier 
should be “setting the agenda.” 

That is the core political idea behind Laude.

It is not democratic control of AI.

It is redistribution of AI agenda-setting power
within a select elite technical class.

Instead of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and a 
few other corporations monopolizing the
frontier, Konwinski wants universities, 
elite researchers, technical founders,
philanthropists and selected public institutions
to possess enough resources to compete with them.

Selected by him.

That may decentralize technical capability. 

It does not decentralize social decision-making
to the population at large.

The distinction is visible in the foundational
"Shaping AI’s Impact on Billions of Lives"
paper. 

The authors explicitly say computer scientists
should take a more active role in
steering AI research and its social impact. 

They assume that AI development will 
continue or accelerate. 

Their proposed response is then to direct that
development toward "chosen" social objectives
through prizes, research centers, public-private
partnerships and philanthropic capital from
technologists. 

The employment section is particularly revealing. 

The paper does not begin from the question of 
whether workers want particular
forms of automation. 

It begins from expected disruption
and asks how workers can adapt. 

It explicitly rejects government subsidy
as the long-term solution  and proposes rapid
upskilling and a Job Forecaster that directs
displaced workers toward growing occupations. 

The #Stanford project now implements that logic. 

It will measure changing jobs and skills, 
use payroll-provider partnerships
to detect emerging demand, 
study human-AI collaboration, 
and develop systems are supposed to help people
learn what the future labor market requires. 

Laude describes the question as how to “prepare people for what comes next.” 

Notice the direction of adaptation.

The technological-economic transition is treated
as the big moving object.

The worker is just an insignificant object that must be 
prepared for it.

That is already a substantive ideology 
of technological change, even though
it is presented as pragmatic research.

The alternative question would be whether
workers should participate in deciding
which technological-economic changes 
occur in the first place. 

The agenda is to build an alternative center
of AI power around open research,
elite computer scientists, technical founders
and philanthropic capital; 
to accelerate research into deployed systems; 
to shape research incentives around 
measurable “impact”; 
and to move academic discoveries more rapidly
into society and,  where appropriate, companies.

The research side and venture side correspond
almost perfectly to different stages of the same
worldview.

Laude Institute says: "ship your research."

Laude Ventures says: turn technical breakthroughs into "breakout companies"

Moonshots adds another layer:
choose civilization-scale problems and mobilize "elite" 
researchers to solve them.

Open Frontier adds another: 
construct an independent technical power center
capable of competing with closed frontier laboratories.

The entire architecture expresses one 
underlying conviction:

Technically "exceptional" people should have
substantially more power to determine 
technological development and its social application.

Konwinski does not conceal that conviction. 

Laude states it explicitly.

The reflexivity problem

This is where his July essay becomes revealing.

Konwinski correctly identifies a governance problem
when several corporations acquire the practical ability
to determine which AI work is possible. 

He writes that participation at the frontier increasingly
depends on permission from a small number
of private organizations. 

But his proposed solution does not ask
why the technical elite should possess
this authority either.

It just changes the identity of the gatekeepers.

The frontier companies become the wrong
concentration of expertise and capital.

The research commons becomes the right
concentration of expertise and capital.

What is missing is the recursive application
of his own argument:

If concentrated actors should not decide which AI
futures everyone else receives,
why should 
Konwinski, 
Laude, 
its donors, 
its selection committee
and a network of 
highly credentialed researchers
possess that authority?

Laude’s own selection procedure demonstrates
the problem. 

The first Moonshots committee emphasized
Turing Award winners,  Nobel laureates, 
famous computer scientists, technology executives,
economists, medical experts and policy figures. 

The published committee description does
not identify ANY organized labor or worker representatives as a corresponding source
of authority over the workforce agenda. 

Affected people appear later. Much later.

As test subjects; not human beings.

Researchers can interview them. 
Projects can test systems on them. 
Workers can supply feedback. 
Communities can participate in pilots.

But the agenda has already been constructed upstream.

Konwinski and collaborators selected
the four problem domains. 
Laude selected the committee.
The committee selected the projects.
Laude supplied the money.
Then, remarkably, NSF supplied $17 million toward
three labs selected through the Laude process, 
subject to additional agency review.

Private agenda formation therefore acquired 
public funding.

That is significant institutional power.

Why should Konwinski be setting this agenda?

No democratic justification has been supplied.

The justification offered is essentially competence:
Konwinski has built important technology; 
Dave Patterson and the researchers
around him have extraordinary technical records;
therefore they are presumed capable of identifying
important problems and directing technical
resources toward solutions.

That establishes technical credibility.

It does not establish political legitimacy.

Konwinski’s documented expertise is computer science,
AI, distributed systems, technical startups and venture
investment.

Nothing in the public record establishes equivalent
expertise in labor relations, working-class institutions,
organized labor, vocational systems, industrial sociology
or the lived organization of ordinary workplaces.

Yet his money and institutions allow him to participate
in deciding how workers should adapt to AI.

That asymmetry is the central issue.

His $100 million pledge gives him something
an ordinary warehouse worker,
nurse, accountant, designer, teacher, driver 
or administrative employee does not possess: 

the ability to turn a personal theory about the future
of work into a $10 million Stanford laboratory.

Money therefore becomes agenda-setting capacity.

Technical success becomes epistemic authority.

Philanthropy converts both into institutional legitimacy.

And the resulting institution describes this process
as working on behalf of everyone.

The unanswered question remains exactly Konwinski’s
own question about frontier AI corporations, 
redirected toward his institution:

Who gave them the authority to decide?

The available record supplies no answer beyond wealth,
technical achievement, elite peer recognition, 
and the ability to assemble enough resources 
to make the project happen. 

Those explain how Konwinski acquired the power.

They do not explain why that power should be
considered legitimate.

🌿 What home remedy did your grandparents swear by? Share one in the comments—then see what deserves a place in your prepper toolkit.

Old remedies deserve a safety check. Here are 50 remedies and home-care practices to reconsider, with safer updates where needed. These address minor symptoms and basic first aid; traditional use alone doesn’t prove effectiveness.

50 OLD-SCHOOL REMEDIES & SAFER UPDATES 👇

1️⃣ HONEY FOR COUGHS

May soothe coughing. Never give honey to babies under 12 months.

2️⃣ WARM DRINKS

Comfortably warm water or tea can soothe an irritated throat.

3️⃣ SALTWATER GARGLE

Adults: dissolve ½ teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water. Gargle and spit.

4️⃣ COOL, SOFT FOODS

Soft foods and ice pops can make a sore throat more comfortable.

5️⃣ SALINE NASAL SPRAY

Prepared saline spray or drops can help with stuffy nasal passages.

6️⃣ SAFE NASAL RINSING

Use a proper saline mixture with distilled or sterile water. Follow device instructions.

7️⃣ FENNEL TEA

Certain preparations have traditional use for mild bloating. Clinical evidence is limited; follow labeling.

8️⃣ GINGER

Ginger tea or foods may help nausea. Check pregnancy supplements with a pharmacist.

9️⃣ PEPPERMINT TEA

May help nausea. Skip it if it aggravates your heartburn.

🔟 SMALL, LIGHT MEALS

Smaller portions eaten more frequently may be easier on a queasy stomach.

1️⃣1️⃣ FRESH AIR

A little fresh air may help ease nausea.

1️⃣2️⃣ CARAWAY TEA

A traditional option for mild gas and bloating; reliable clinical evidence remains limited.

1️⃣3️⃣ PRUNES

Prunes or prune juice can help with constipation.

1️⃣4️⃣ RAISINS AND APRICOTS

These fruits supply fiber and sorbitol, which can help soften stools.

1️⃣5️⃣ OATS AND BRAN

Gradually adding these fiber sources may improve bowel regularity.

1️⃣6️⃣ WATER WITH FIBER

Drink sufficient fluids as you increase fiber. Follow any prescribed fluid restrictions.

1️⃣7️⃣ A DAILY WALK

Regular movement can help relieve constipation.

1️⃣8️⃣ A TOILET FOOTSTOOL

Supporting your feet with your knees above your hips may make passing stool easier.

1️⃣9️⃣ AN EARLIER SUPPER

For reflux, finish eating three to four hours before bed.

2️⃣0️⃣ A LOOSER WAISTBAND

Avoid tight clothing around your stomach when heartburn troubles you.

2️⃣1️⃣ SLOW BREATHING

Slow, comfortable breathing can help you relax when pain makes you tense.

2️⃣2️⃣ QUIET REST

Resting in a quiet, dark room may help during a familiar migraine.

2️⃣3️⃣ REGULAR MEALS

Skipping meals can trigger headaches. Keep a regular eating schedule.

2️⃣4️⃣ A COOL FOREHEAD CLOTH

A cool cloth on your head may ease migraine discomfort.

2️⃣5️⃣ A WARM NECK PACK

A comfortably warm, wrapped pack may ease ordinary neck pain. Protect your skin.

2️⃣6️⃣ GENTLE MOVEMENT

Once pain allows, gently move a recovering sprain to help prevent stiffness.

2️⃣7️⃣ A WRAPPED COLD PACK

For a fresh sprain, apply through a cloth for up to 20 minutes.

2️⃣8️⃣ ELEVATION

Support a sprained limb on pillows to help reduce swelling.

2️⃣9️⃣ REST FROM PAINFUL ACTIVITIES

Protect a fresh strain and pause activities that make it hurt.

3️⃣0️⃣ A WARM BATH

Warm water may ease muscle spasm. Avoid heat on fresh, swollen injuries.

3️⃣1️⃣ RUNNING WATER FOR BURNS

Cool a fresh thermal burn under cool running water for 20 minutes. Skip butter, oils, and raw egg.

3️⃣2️⃣ A COOL SUNBURN COMPRESS

Gently apply a cool, damp cloth to sunburned skin.

3️⃣3️⃣ ALOE MOISTURIZER

An aloe-containing moisturizer may soothe mild sunburn on intact skin.

3️⃣4️⃣ COLLOIDAL OATMEAL

A colloidal oatmeal bath can soothe itchy, sunburned skin.

3️⃣5️⃣ CALAMINE LOTION

Use as labeled for itching and sunburn discomfort.

3️⃣6️⃣ DIRECT PRESSURE

Press firmly on a bleeding cut with clean gauze. Uncontrolled bleeding needs emergency help.

3️⃣7️⃣ CLEAN-WATER WOUND RINSING

Rinse minor cuts with clean running water. Keep kitchen ingredients out of wounds.

3️⃣8️⃣ PLAIN PETROLEUM JELLY

A thin layer on a clean minor cut helps keep it moist.

3️⃣9️⃣ A CLEAN COVERING

Cover minor cuts and change the dressing when wet or dirty.

4️⃣0️⃣ A COLD CLOTH FOR BITES

A clean, cold cloth can help reduce swelling from an ordinary insect bite.

4️⃣1️⃣ A WARM COMPRESS FOR BOILS

Hold a clean, warm cloth against a small boil. Don’t squeeze it; fever or facial boils need medical advice.

4️⃣2️⃣ FREQUENT DRINKS DURING FEVER

Drink enough to avoid dehydration, following any prescribed fluid restrictions.

4️⃣3️⃣ REST DURING FEVER

Give yourself time to recover. A worsening or persistent fever needs medical advice.

4️⃣4️⃣ A REGULAR WAKE-UP TIME

Getting up at the same time daily supports a steadier sleep routine.

4️⃣5️⃣ A DARK, QUIET BEDROOM

Reduce light and noise when sleep is difficult.

4️⃣6️⃣ LEMON BALM

Traditionally used for mild stress and sleep complaints. Clinical evidence remains limited.

4️⃣7️⃣ CHAMOMILE TEA

A caffeine-free evening option. Related plant allergies can increase reaction risk; medication interactions are possible.

4️⃣8️⃣ A SALTWATER DENTAL RINSE

Adults can gently rinse and spit for temporary comfort while arranging dental care.

4️⃣9️⃣ SOFT FOODS FOR TOOTH PAIN

Choose soft foods and avoid chewing on the painful tooth.

5️⃣0️⃣ LABELED CLOVE-OIL DENTAL PRODUCTS

For adults, these may offer temporary toothache relief. Follow instructions, avoid gum contact, and see a dentist.

🎯 Prepper tip: Keep a small reference card with each remedy’s purpose, preparation, age limits, and warning signs. Check herbal products with a pharmacist, especially during pregnancy or when taking medication.

Get urgent medical help for breathing trouble, uncontrolled bleeding, serious burns, or a sudden, extremely painful headache.

text:
12 Serious Sins Catholics Must Confess Before Receiving Holy Communion 👇

Just because we attend Mass does not mean we should automatically receive Holy Communion.

The Eucharist is not ordinary bread. It is Jesus Christ Himself, truly present in His Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity.

And because of this, the Catholic Church teaches that we must approach Him with reverence, humility, and a soul in a state of grace.

St. Paul gave Christians a serious warning:

→ “Whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of profaning the body and blood of the Lord.” (1 Corinthians 11:27)

This is why Catholics who are aware of having committed a mortal sin must ordinarily go to Confession before receiving Holy Communion.

But there is something important we need to understand.

Not every serious sin is automatically a mortal sin.

For a sin to be mortal, three conditions must be present:

→ Grave matter: The action is seriously wrong.

→ Full knowledge: You understand that what you are doing is gravely sinful.

→ Deliberate consent: You freely choose to commit the sin.

All three conditions must be present for a sin to be mortal.

With that in mind, here are 12 serious sins and situations every Catholic should consider when examining their conscience before receiving the Eucharist.

1. Intentionally Missing Sunday Mass

→ Choosing to skip Sunday Mass or a Holy Day of Obligation without a serious reason, simply because you would rather sleep in, go shopping, or do something else.

2. Receiving Holy Communion in Mortal Sin

→ Knowingly receiving the Eucharist while in a state of mortal sin, or deliberately treating the Blessed Sacrament with grave disrespect or desecrating it.

3. Sexual Sins

→ Engaging in pornography, masturbation, adultery, fornication, or other sexual acts contrary to the Church's moral teachings.

4. Living Together in a Sexual Relationship Outside Marriage

→ Living as husband and wife and engaging in sexual relations without a valid marriage. Simply living under the same roof does not automatically mean someone is committing mortal sin.

5. Intentionally Using Contraception

→ Deliberately preventing conception through contraception, including condoms, contraceptive pills, IUDs, or other methods used for that purpose.

6. Abortion

→ Deliberately obtaining an abortion, encouraging another person to have one, or knowingly cooperating in bringing one about.

7. Murder or Other Serious Acts Against Human Life

→ Intentionally taking an innocent human life, participating in euthanasia, or committing grave acts of violence or abuse against another person.

8. Stealing Something of Serious Value

→ Taking money, property, or possessions that belong to someone else, especially when the theft causes significant financial loss or harm.

9. Serious Injustice Toward Others

→ Cheating workers out of fair wages, exploiting vulnerable people, spreading lies that seriously damage someone's reputation, engaging in corruption, or abusing positions of authority.

10. Deliberately Refusing to Pay Serious Debts

→ Choosing not to repay money you rightfully owe when you have the means and moral responsibility to do so.

11. Holding On to Serious Hatred or Revenge

→ Deliberately wishing grave harm upon another person, feeding hatred, or planning revenge.

Forgiving someone does not mean pretending their actions were acceptable or allowing them to continue hurting you.

12. Serious Sins Caused by Pride, Greed, Envy, or Sloth

→ Allowing these vices to lead you into grave wrongdoing, such as deliberately neglecting important responsibilities, causing serious harm through selfishness, or ruining another person's reputation out of jealousy.

Now, here is something every Catholic needs to remember.

The Church does not teach us to examine our conscience because Jesus wants us to be terrified of approaching Him.

She teaches us this because sin is serious, and our relationship with God matters.

At the Last Supper, when Peter resisted having his feet washed, Jesus told him:

→ “If I do not wash you, you have no part in me.” (John 13:8)

Although Jesus was teaching His disciples about humble service, His words also remind us of our need to be cleansed by Him.

And that is exactly why the Sacrament of Confession is such an incredible gift.

When we fall into mortal sin, God does not stop calling us back.

He offers us forgiveness.

Through a sincere Confession, with true repentance and sacramental absolution, our sins are forgiven, sanctifying grace is restored, and we are reconciled with God and His Church.

But there is also a serious warning we cannot ignore.

Deliberately receiving Holy Communion while knowing we are in a state of mortal sin is itself another grave sin called sacrilege.

That is why we should never approach the Eucharist as though receiving Jesus were simply another part of our Sunday routine.

We are receiving the Lord Himself.

And He deserves more than a casual approach.

He deserves our love, our reverence, and hearts willing to turn away from sin.

Remember, committing an act involving grave matter does not automatically mean a person has committed mortal sin. Full knowledge and deliberate consent are also necessary.

If you are unsure about your spiritual state, seek guidance from a priest rather than trying to judge everything on your own.

And if you know you have fallen into mortal sin, do not despair.

Go to Confession. Return to Jesus. His mercy is greater than your sins.

The purpose of all this is not to keep you away from the Eucharist forever.

It is to help you receive Jesus worthily, with a heart prepared to welcome Him.

💬 Do you believe Catholics today are being taught clearly enough about mortal sin, Confession, and the importance of receiving Holy Communion in a state of grace?

text:
AGNIPATH'S SECOND U-TURN: NATIONAL SECURITY CANNOT BE RUN AS AN EXPERIMENT IN POLITICAL DAMAGE CONTROL

Is the government correcting a flawed military recruitment policy, or merely postponing the consequences of a decision that has left thousands of young aspirants uncertain about their future?

SOURCE & ATTRIBUTION

Y. Shivam — YouTube investigative analysis, November 8, 2026.

 [https://t.co/ig9k4PqvTy]

THE CENTRAL CONTRADICTION

On November 4, 2026, the Union Cabinet approved a two-year extension of service for Agniveers, alongside a pathway for eligible and willing personnel to enter the regular Army after completing four or six years.

This is a significant change to the original Agnipath framework, which recruited young people for four years and provided for only 25% to be retained in the regular cadre.

The obvious question is: if the original arrangement was so well designed, why does it require another major adjustment?

THE POLICY'S SECOND U-TURN

THE NUMBERS BEHIND THE CONCERN

The government's explanation is that the extension follows four years of performance assessment and feedback from the armed forces. The remaining 75% will receive two additional years of engagement, after which they will be offered regular enrolment, subject to willingness and selection criteria. Importantly, this is not an unconditional guarantee of permanent employment. Press Information Bureau

Meanwhile, the 19th Parliamentary Standing Committee on Defence confirms that Defence R&D's share of the defence budget has declined from 5.9% in 2021–22 to 5% in 2026–27. Its allocation has increased in absolute terms, but its proportion has fallen. 19TH REPORT DFG (2026-27)

THE UNANSWERED QUESTIONS

Why was a policy presented as essential to military modernisation revised so substantially after four years?

What happens to those who fail the eventual selection criteria?

Are the promised employment opportunities in paramilitary forces and state police backed by adequate vacancies and implementation?

And why should young people planning their lives around military service bear the uncertainty of repeated policy changes?

The video's suggestion that the December 2028 timeline is linked to electoral calculations is an allegation, not an established fact. It deserves scrutiny, not automatic acceptance.

NATIONAL SECURITY IS NOT AN EXPERIMENTAL PLAYGROUND. Soldiers deserve dignity, predictable careers and institutional security. Defence modernisation requires sustained investment in technology, research and trained personnel—not merely changes to recruitment arithmetic.

A GOVERNMENT MAY REVISE A POLICY, BUT IT MUST ANSWER FOR THE HUMAN COST OF GETTING IT WRONG.

The instructions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) were NOT formulated in this way. The phrase “Outbreed, then conquer, then kill anyone who doesn’t submit” is a modern polemical summary; it does not appear in this form in either the Qur’an or the authentic hadiths.

His actual instructions regarding warfare and non-Muslims
When the Prophet sent out an army or a detachment, he would give the commanders the following basic instructions (reported in Sahih Muslim and other sources):

Fear Allah and treat the Muslims well.
Do not act treacherously, do not steal from the spoils of war, do not mutilate the dead, and do not kill children.
When you meet your polytheist enemy, offer them three things:
Invite them to Islam. If they accept, leave them.
If they refuse, demand the jizya (poll tax). If they pay it, leave them.
If they refuse both, then fight them.⁠Sunnah
The killing of women, children, and the elderly (non-combatants) was also explicitly forbidden. On one occasion, when he saw a woman who had been killed, he asked “Who killed her?” and prohibited the killing of women and children (Bukhari and Muslim).⁠Tohed

The hadith “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say ‘La ilaha illallah’…” (Bukhari and Muslim) is authentic. However, it was said in the context of the Arab polytheists, most of whom were actively hostile, and after the invitation to Islam. Once someone utters the testimony of faith, their life and property are protected. There is also the verse “There is no compulsion in religion” (Al-Baqarah 256) and the command to accept peace if it is offered (Al-Anfal 61).

What does not exist
There is no instruction about “outbreeding” (overcoming through higher birth rates). No strategic command regarding birth rates appears in the hadiths. This is entirely a product of modern demographic discussions.
There is no general order to “kill anyone who does not submit.” Non-combatant women, children, the elderly, monks, etc., are protected. People of the Book (Jews and Christians) were given dhimmi status in exchange for the jizya. Treaties were made with Jews in Medina, and peace offers were accepted.
In summary: The Prophet’s rules of war, in the conditions of his time, consist of the sequence invitation → jizya → fighting and the protection of civilians/non-combatants. The three-stage slogan “outbreed, conquer, kill those who do not submit” is not an accurate summary of his instructions.

text:
Kim, I'm writing to offer the cheapest commodity in politics: advice.
But as a veteran of not one but two Ohio GOP insurgencies, I speak with some experience.
1. Judge Alex will not resign. He'll dig in. He's almost certainly been working the phones since Tuesday night, making sure he has the 34 votes to keep himself in business.
Think about it, Kim. Earlier this year everyone knew it was going to be difficult. One of two solid candidates, Tressel or Yost, would have done well in a Catholic and Evangelical working-class state. Yet the state GOP thought it better to elevate a Hindu techie without so much as a public vote on the matter. This was a monstrous blunder, born of arrogance. Those responsible are now blaming others for the disaster. Resignation? Not a chance.
The good news is that arrogance and idiocy is a debilitating combination. Which means it's beatable.
2. GOP officials hang on to their posts because it benefits them personally in the way of prestige or influence, and sometimes health insurance and an income stream. Electing Republicans is someone else's job. 
3. The GOP is not a party. It's a club. And if you're reading this, you're not in it.
4. I've complained for years that endorsements do nothing but promote weak candidates and repel new volunteers and donors. They only enhance the prestige of otherwise unremarkable committee people who just want to remain the club. Which of course is why weak parties endorse.
About those takeover efforts mentioned above: they started energetically, expanded rapidly and then failed spectacularly after we were betrayed by people we mistakenly trusted. The same tragedy will befall anyone else who tries. So don't.
The Republican election system is broken. It cannot be fixed. That's because a) those in charge have the votes to prevent a fix, and b) history has demonstrated that a campaign to gain the votes is a fools errand. (Unfortunately I was the fool who performed the demonstration.)
The solution is to form a completely different political organization, an entirely volunteer group that parallels the Republican structure. This group would 
-- Form a charter and elect its leaders
-- Raise its own money, both from new donors and traditional GOP givers.
-- Recruit candidates who can win in November and not just in May. Train them, perhaps start them with seed money and promote them through the primary.
In some ways this would be similar to TPUSA, except that the organization would be unmistakably Republican, which creates some funding restrictions. Someone suggested it would be more like the Conservative Party in New York. Sort of, but not a statutory party.
Now is the time to make this happen because, after Tuesday's disaster, more people realize something needs to change. And are looking for answers.
My associates (some would say confederates) and I are hashing this out. (In fact there's a meeting Monday night.) If you wish to learn more, you know how to reach me.
You will be welcomed to the revolution.

text:
DECKERS $DECK ROSE 5.8% AND LOST 12 PLACES:

Deckers Brands (DECK) at $86.71, -$1.03 / -1.17% on Friday.

Deckers slipped to #28 on the Quality-Value Len5 as its shares rose, and neither development we said would cost it the seat has happened. The whole rise came on two days when oil fell hard and consumer stocks climbed together, with nothing from Deckers behind it. Two analysts cut their price targets into that rise anyway. Deckers heads into the holiday quarter with inventory growing no faster than sales and a share count 8% smaller than a year ago. On Holding (ONON), the running-shoe maker HOKA competes with most directly, reports on Tuesday, and its September quarter is the earliest look at whether HOKA's slowdown belongs to HOKA alone.

Deckers is #28 of 80 on the Quality-Value Len5, from #16 when we flagged it. Quality-Value wants a durable business at a discount, and Deckers's discount is now 11.5 times the $7.54 a share it earned over the past four quarters, from 10.9 times in our post. We named two things that would knock it off the Quality-Value Len5, and both still stand: HOKA holiday-quarter sales below the year before, or the shares back above $110 on the same forecast. Neither has happened. Our read: the seat moved because the price did, with nothing new from Deckers behind it. It is on none of the Momentum, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es; Momentum wants a stock near its high, and Friday's close is 29.1% under the $122.29 Deckers touched on February 20. It still passes the Quality Len5, profitable with no borrowings and $1.21B of cash at September 30.

Nothing from Deckers moved the shares this week; its only news was UGG's holiday campaign, launched November 2. Oil did the moving, twice, and consumer stocks rose together both times.
- Since our post: +$4.72 / +5.8% from the $81.99 close we quoted, about $630M of market value.
- United States Oil Fund (USO), which tracks the price of US crude, at $148.41, +$0.20 / +0.13% on Friday. Since our post: -12.1%.
- Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY) at $117.58, -$0.06 / -0.05% on Friday. Since our post: +1.9%.
- SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) at $735.29, +$2.29 / +0.31% on Friday. Since our post: -2.7%.
- Monday, November 2: the oil fund -7.1% after IRNA, Iran's state news agency, reported that Iran would pursue negotiations with Washington. Deckers +3.7%; the consumer fund +2.4%.
- Wednesday, November 4, the day after Democrats won both houses of Congress: the oil fund -8.1%. Deckers +6.0%; the consumer fund +4.3%; the market fund +1.7%.
- Thursday, November 5: the market fund -4.4%. Deckers -1.5%.
Our read: buyers treated cheaper oil as cheaper gasoline, and cheaper gasoline as holiday money for shoppers, and Deckers rose with the group.

Two analysts cut their targets into the rise. Aneesha Sherman of Bernstein went to $100 from $105 on November 3 and kept a Hold rating; Christine Dooley of Argus Research went to $102 from $128 this week and kept her Buy. Both targets sit above Friday's close.

Deckers stocked for the holidays in step with its sales, and the buyback kept taking shares out:
- Inventory at September 30: $860.8M, +3.0% from a year earlier. Sales in the quarter: +3.5%.
- Shares outstanding on October 8: 133.5M, from 145.7M a year earlier, -8.4%.
- Buyback authorization left, the amount the board has approved for repurchases: $4.41B, about 38% of Deckers's $11.6B market value.

On Holding (ONON) at $37.36, -$0.18 / -0.48% on Friday, HOKA's closest rival in cushioned running shoes, reports its September quarter on Tuesday, November 10, before the open, eleven weeks before Deckers reports. On's sales grew 13.5% as reported and 21.6% in constant currency, which strips out swings in exchange rates, in the June quarter, against HOKA's 7.7% over the same months. Deckers's US sales fell 0.4% in the September quarter, and On's Americas sales for those same months arrive Tuesday, after growing 13.0% in constant currency in the June quarter. A quarter near On's own full-year pace, constant-currency growth in the low 20s, would say the slowdown is HOKA's; one well under it would say running shoes slowed as a category. On is up 10.6% since our post, and it is on none of the Len5es we weigh; at about 25 times the past year's profit it offers no discount for the two value Len5es.

Deckers keeps its Quality-Value seat on a smaller discount, after a week that cheaper oil made and HOKA had no part in. Tuesday's On report is the first reading on whether running shoes slowed with HOKA or around it. Deckers answers for HOKA's own holiday with the December quarter, tentatively reported January 28.

text: While Bitcoin is struggling around $75,000, something much bigger is happening in Washington. A rule that could open America's $10.8 trillion 401(k) retirement market to crypto has reached the White House for final review. Think about that for a second. Even a hypothetical 1% allocation would represent $108 billion. But what interests me isn't just the money. We're watching crypto move from something institutions once warned people against into something they may eventually offer inside retirement portfolios. And that raises a serious question. Is Bitcoin mature enough to become part of someone's retirement savings, or are we moving too fast? I believe institutional adoption matters, but retirement money deserves a completely different level of responsibility than speculative trading. The rule isn't approved yet, and nobody is required to buy crypto. Still, I think this could become one of the most important regulatory developments for Bitcoin in years. #VOLF #Bitcoin #BTC #Crypto #Web3 #ORINBIX

text:
NFL Week 9 Injury Report: DraftKings Main Slate DFS Impact | November 8

The injury news that can change Sunday’s DFS slate:

1️⃣ SEAHAWKS: Darnold and Shaheed OUT

Drew Lock ($4,000) starts. JSN ($9,300) and Cooper Kupp ($3,800) are the receiving options. LT Charles Cross and LG Quenton Nelson are also out, so protection is a real concern for Seattle stacks.

2️⃣ TEXANS: David Montgomery OUT

Woody Marks ($5,700) gets a clearer opportunity and remains a strong midrange RB consideration. The absence creates upside, though the exact workload still has to play out.

3️⃣ PATRIOTS: A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson OUT; Hunter Henry QUESTIONABLE

Rhamondre Stevenson ($6,100) has less backfield competition. DeMario Douglas ($4,800) and Efton Chism III ($3,600) are receiving options. Mack Hollins has been activated, adding target competition. Henry’s status matters for the tight-end rotation.

4️⃣ JETS: Garrett Wilson OUT

Adonai Mitchell ($4,500) gets an expanded receiving opportunity and makes sense as a bring-back in Kansas City passing builds. Patrick Mahomes + Rashee Rice + Mitchell costs $17,000.

5️⃣ GIANTS: Cam Skattebo DOUBTFUL; Malik Nabers cleared

Devin Singletary ($4,600) becomes more appealing if Skattebo is inactive. Nabers practiced fully Friday and has no game designation.

6️⃣ EAGLES: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Britain Covey OUT

Joe Milton III ($4,100) is set for his first NFL start with a depleted receiving group. Saquon Barkley ($6,200) practiced fully Friday and has no game designation. The cheap QB opens salary but carries significant uncertainty.

7️⃣ LIONS: Amon-Ra St. Brown QUESTIONABLE

St. Brown ($8,100) was limited all week with a rib injury. If he sits, reassess Jameson Williams ($6,100) and Jahmyr Gibbs ($10,000) for passing-game opportunity. Center Cade Mays is also out.

8️⃣ DOLPHINS: Malik Willis cleared; Detroit defense depleted

Willis ($5,100) has no game designation. Detroit has ruled out Jack Campbell, Kerby Joseph, D.J. Reed and DJ Wonnum, strengthening the matchup case for Miami passing options, including Greg Dulcich ($3,100).

9️⃣ COMMANDERS: Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks OUT

Antonio Williams ($4,100) provides salary relief. Stefon Diggs ($5,600) costs $1,500 more and offers a different receiving and scoring path. Both deserve consideration in Washington builds.

🔟 RAMS: Terrance Ferguson OUT; Colby Parkinson QUESTIONABLE

Tyler Higbee ($3,700) has no game designation and becomes more interesting if Parkinson sits. On defense, Jaylen Watson is out; Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, relevant to Washington stacks.

1️⃣1️⃣ BRONCOS: Pat Bryant QUESTIONABLE

Bryant ($3,700) is questionable despite full practices. Jaylen Waddle ($5,700) and Courtland Sutton ($4,400) have no game designation. Reassess the receiver rotation if Bryant sits.

1️⃣2️⃣ SAINTS: Jordyn Tyson QUESTIONABLE; Alvin Kamara cleared

Tyson ($5,200) remains questionable after three limited practices. Chris Olave ($7,400) is the established receiver to compare against that uncertainty. Kamara ($5,000) has no game designation; CJ Donaldson is out.

1️⃣3️⃣ 49ERS: Evans, Deebo and Kirk OUT; CMC cleared

Christian McCaffrey ($8,000) and George Kittle ($6,000) remain established receiving options. Demarcus Robinson ($4,300) was activated and cleared, adding competition for Jordan Watkins ($3,300).

1️⃣4️⃣ COWBOYS: Ferguson, Schoonmaker and Pickens QUESTIONABLE

Brevyn Spann-Ford ($2,900) becomes a more relevant value TE if both Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker sit. George Pickens’ status also affects the passing-game outlook. Don’t assume those absences before inactives.

text:
SpaceX pulled off an $85.7 billion IPO earlier this summer, but it floated only around 5% of its total shares for public trading. Most tech giants offer 15% to 20% right out of the gate, while Saudi Aramco raised $25.6 billion with a 1.5% float. Keeping the public float that tight came with a real cost.

The S&P 500 typically demands at least a 10% float, and SpaceX saw its application for fast-track inclusion flatly denied. The thin supply also fueled wild price swings in early trading. Now the floodgates are opening.

Another 20% of shares freed up after second-quarter earnings in August, and October third-quarter results unlocked an additional 28%. The next massive block becomes eligible to trade on December 9, marking one of the biggest share unlock events in IPO history. The artificial scarcity phase is over, and the market is about to see real supply meet real demand.

A nearly full friendship bar can be misleading. Some people still need a conversation, a return visit or a fight before their entry is actually finished. Check Diligence Records, then Friendships (Shops), instead of judging it by the bar alone.

These are the 24 shop friendships in the 2023 remake. The other 23 bonds are listed separately under Friendships.

When somebody asks you to come back, leave and reload the area before returning. Entering and leaving Teradaya is a useful reset. Buying ten things in one transaction also isn't always the same as making ten visits, so watch whether the bar moves.

FUSHIMI

• Utamaruya Owner: At the singing bar on North Fushimi Ichibangai. Sing, end the session and speak to him again rather than continually extending the same session. Keep returning through the trouble with his customers. When the bar shuts down, leave and come back, then beat the men involved.

• Umai Udon Owner: At Umai Udon on Fushimi Ichibangai. Buy meals and work the udon-serving minigame once it opens. Keep going until the job-offer conversation finishes the bond. The minigame's sales targets are separate requirements.

• Fukufuku Pub Owner: Buy drinks at Fukufuku on Fushimi Ichibangai. When his usual sake becomes unavailable, leave and return. Tell him “No, it's fine,” then “Water would taste better” during the tasting conversation.

• Ichikura Owner: Buy individual items at Ichikura General Goods on Fushimi Ichibangai. Cheap purchases work. Eventually a shoplifter runs off; catch him to finish.

• Greengrocer: Buy vegetables from the Fushimi Ichibangai stall. When he requests help, bring him 10 carrots.

RAKUNAI

• Maijo-sensei: At Nichibuza on Kawaramachi, after Substory 1. Take dance lessons until she arranges the competition. Complete Fubuki Kouta on Geisha difficulty for the final event.

• Shinto Priest: At the shrine on Karasuma Street. Purchase the Virtue Exchange upgrade at a shrine, then trade with him. Finish by chasing the thief and checking the hiding places if you lose sight of him.

• Akari: At the same shrine from Chapter 4. Talk, leave and return for more conversations. Bring medicine when she gets sick, then return for the remaining scene. Her question about Haruka doesn't require a particular answer.

• Hanamaru Udon Employee: Eat at Hanamaru Udon on East Shijo Street. Continue until he creates his special Beef Udon. Remember to order that new dish too if you're completing the restaurant menu.

• Shogi Parlor Owner: Play at the parlor on Shinmeicho. Keep speaking to the owner between games. His final opponent doesn't have to be beaten to finish the friendship; the separate shogi win requirement still does.

• Sushi Zanmai Chef: Eat at Sushi Zanmai on Kawaramachi. After the special-tuna invitation, leave and return for that meal.

• Ecchudo Apothecary: Visit Ecchudo on Kawaramachi and test his medicine. Return between experiments, and don't arrive at full health when he needs an injured test subject. One experiment leaves you in terrible shape, so heal before wandering into street fights. Finishing unlocks Longevity Pills for 8,000 mon each, restoring health and Heat.

• Don Quijote Employee: Shop at Don Quijote on Shijo Street. Follow the customer's request outside, check the rice bales by the shop's southern wall, then report back.

• Ebisu Pawnbroker: Use the Rakunai branch on East Shijo Street. Buy or sell until he needs a customer. Find the antique seller near Fermented Goods on Shinmeicho, send him over, then return to the pawnbroker.

• Momokawa Brothers: Eat at Shippoku Momokawa on East Shijo Street. Continue through their cooking competition and judge the dishes. Either choice finishes their event.

RAKUGAI

• Cho-Han Dealer: At the Gambling Den on Sannocho. Play, then approach the exit to start the bond. Keep ending your session after a round and talking again. Save before the final 10-ryo wager and aim to win it.

• Chicken Race Receptionist: At the racing den on Umekojicho. Watch races and leave between visits; placing a bet isn't necessary for the friendship itself. Return through his losing and winning streaks, then choose either bird when he asks for advice.

• Uji Tea Parlor Girl: Buy food or drinks at Uji Tea Parlor on West Umekojicho. After she discusses her boyfriend, leave and return. Defeat him when he causes trouble.

• Rakugai Arms Dealer: Southeast of Uji Tea Parlor. Make separate purchases; cheap Bundle Blades work. Answer his questions however you like. Finishing earns a Dragon Fang and adds Worn Swords to his stock.

MUKUROGAI

• Mahjong House Residents: At Mahjong Spot on the southwestern ground floor. You need 25,000 sticks to enter a game. Start a game, quit if necessary, then walk toward the building's exit for the conversation. Repeat. When those conversations stop, leave the area and return for the Advanced Table invitation. Starting that game counts even if you quit. Actual mahjong completion goals are another matter.

GION

• Anna: At Yamabuki. Spend time with her playing the courtesan minigames until the bond fills. Don't confuse this with clearing every required difficulty.

• Kasuga Okami: Eat and drink at Kasuga until the troublesome customer appears. Deal with him to finish.

• Kitchen Aoba Chef: Eat at Kitchen Aoba in southern Gion. Accept his special dish, choose whichever response you want, then return and eat again.

AROUND KYO

• Palanquin Bearer: Use the city's palanquins repeatedly. Defeat the bandits when the event triggers. This adds the Sannocho stop in Rakugai, handy for reaching the Gambling Den.

Before moving on, check for all 24 completed entries. A friendship can be finished while the associated restaurant menu or minigame still has work left, so check those records separately.

text:
✨🪔🪷 Dipanwita Puja refers to the worship rituals performed on the darkest night of the year, Kartika Amavasya (Diwali night). While the rest of India focuses primarily on Diwali Lakshmi Puja, the regional tradition in Bengal holds a dual nature. It is heavily celebrated as Dipanwita Kali Puja (Shyama Puja), but also secretly preserves an ancient domestic ritual known as Dipanwita Lakshmi Puja, focused on driving out poverty and welcoming prosperity. 🪷🪔✨

The primary distinction is that while Bengalis worship the universal, household Lakshmi during the full moon of Kojagari Purnima, the Amavasya night is reserved for confronting the dark forces of the universe—both through the fierce grace of Maa Kali and the ritual expulsion of Alakshmi (the goddess of misfortune).

1. The Dual Aspects of Dipanwita Night
Depending on the household lineage (Shakta or Vaishnava), families focus on one or both paths during this night:
Primary Deity: Maa Kali (Dakshina Kali or Bhuvanmohini) <-> Dhanalakshmi / Mahalakshmi
Core Intent: Overcoming cosmic illusion, fear, and evil <-> Banishing poverty and inviting wealth
Timing: Midnight (Nishita Kaal) <-> Dusk/Evening (Pradosh Kaal)
Key Offering: Red Hibiscus, Khichuri, symbolic sacrifice <-> Sweets, batasa, whole coriander, coconut

2. Ritual Steps for Household Dipanwita Lakshmi Puja
For families that observe the domestic Lakshmi puja on Diwali night, the process follows a strict progression of driving away bad luck before welcoming wealth.

Alakshmi Biday (Expulsion of Misfortune): This is the mandatory precursor. An idol of Alakshmi is crafted out of cow dung. She is "worshipped" with absolute disdain—offered non-refined items like fruit peels, and lit with kerosene or cheap oils instead of ghee. The idol is then placed on a banana sheath, dragged out of the house to a crossroads, and left behind.
The Cleansing Noise: As Alakshmi is thrown out, family members beat old tin cans or winnowing fans (kulo) with sticks. This loud, harsh sound is meant to scare away the lingering energies of poverty, bad luck, and arguments from the house.
Ghat Sthapana & Welcome: Once the negative energy is cast out, the house is purified with Ganga water. A sacred copper or clay ghat (pot) is established for Lakshmi. A whole fruit (like a raw coconut or wood apple) is placed on top to ensure wealth never depletes.
Pituli Worship: In traditional homes, small clay or rice-paste (pituli) idols representing a red Lakshmi, a blue Narayana, and a green Kuber are worshipped together.
Deep Daan (Festival of Lamps): Ghee or mustard oil lamps are lit around the altar and every corner of the house to guide the feet of Dhanalakshmi into the home.

text:
Another big week of cloud compute news.

I summarized everything from Railway, AWS, Crusoe, GCP, DigitalOcean, Render, Vultr, and more...

1/ @awscloud expanded WorkSpaces for AI agents to support Linux and Windows 11 cloud desktops.

- Their new service supports Linux and Windows 11 environments, giving agents access to desktop applications.

2/ @googlecloud made their dated Compute Engine API versions generally available

- Developers can target a specific API version, making infrastructure integrations more predictable as the platform evolves.

- Google also acquired @CrusoeAI's southeast Wyoming data center site.

3/ @digitalocean took another step into the AI agent space, with Secrets Manager in public preview

- It gives teams a dedicated place to manage application secrets. 

4/ @render launched Sandboxes in public beta

- Each sandbox runs in a Firecracker microVM with an outbound firewall. They also added support for API-key injection outside the sandbox, which is in early access.

5/ @vercel made tracing generally available across all plans

- This gives developers more visibility into application execution, helping them investigate latency and failures beyond what individual log lines reveal.

6/ @railway faced a PR nightmare over unauthorized testing, and separately faced IP issues

- @joshmanders posted logs that show a Railway employee's agent attempted to access secrets and scan @primcloud's internal network. He says the attempts were blocked. Railway's CEO said the employee independently ran a personal bug-bounty tool (which Josh says his platform does not offer) against one external provider and that Railway doesn't condone the actions.

- Some network providers blocked Railway IPs. Railway attributes this to scanning traffic with forged source IPs and says it found no link to October's breach. Recovery remains partial.

7/ @Vultr announced a 20 MW AMD GPU cluster in 🇮🇳Chennai 

8/ Northflank published updates on its security breach

- Attackers decrypted control-plane secrets, and customers reported unauthorized use of AI API keys. Northflank revised the timeline this week, placing the first decryption ~9 hours before its initial alert.

- Running workloads were unaffected. Customers on dedicated or forward-deployed control planes weren't exposed, according to Northflank. Root-cause analysis remains pending.

text:
Well, ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, and assorted reprobates who have somehow managed to tolerate my particular brand of insanity over the years...
I have an announcement to make.
Apparently, someone has finally decided that allowing me to spend my working hours surrounded by firearms, ammunition, and people with an equally questionable sense of humor is a perfectly reasonable employment decision.
Yes, you read that correctly. I've got a SECOND job!
Before anyone gets the wrong idea, let me make one thing perfectly clear: I'm still working for Enterprise, and I have no intention of leaving. This is an additional, part-time position that allows me to put another set of skills and qualifications to good use.
I've recently joined the crew at Center Mass in Livonia, Michigan, where I'll be putting my rather extensive background in firearms instruction, range safety, and general firearms knowledge to work.
For those who don't know, I've been an NRA Certified Firearms Instructor for approximately 24 years, and for the past 17 years, I've also been a certified Center Axis Relock (CAR) and IPD Systems Instructor. Add to that my background in defensive firearms techniques, personal protection, Close Protection operations, and threat management, and I've accumulated a fair bit of knowledge and experience over the years.
So, rather than letting all that knowledge gather dust in the increasingly cluttered filing cabinet that passes for my brain, I'm getting the opportunity to put it to work again.
And here's the really interesting part...
I'm thoroughly enjoying it!
The crew at Center Mass are a fantastic bunch of people. Knowledgeable, professional, safety-conscious, and possessed of the sort of thoroughly inappropriate sense of humor that makes me feel right at home.
It's rather refreshing to spend time in an environment where firearms aren't treated as mysterious, terrifying objects, but as tools that demand knowledge, proficiency, discipline, and respect.
Now, here's the shameless promotional bit.
If you're anywhere around Metro Detroit and you're interested in firearms, whether you're a seasoned shooter, someone looking to improve your skills, or a complete beginner who's never fired a shot in your life, I would strongly encourage you to pay Center Mass a visit.
Whether you're looking for some quality range time, firearms and accessories, or knowledgeable people who can help you make informed decisions, it's well worth stopping by.
And finding us couldn't be much easier!
Center Mass is located on Plymouth Road in Livonia, just east of Stark Road, on the south side of the street.
So, if you're in the neighborhood, stop in, have a look around, and see what we've got to offer.
And if you happen to wander through the doors while I'm working, come over and say hello!
I promise to be on my best behavior.
Well... reasonably good behavior.
All right, I'll try not to get fired before I've finished my probationary period.
Center Mass — Plymouth Road, Livonia, Michigan. Just east of Stark Road, on the south side.
Come for the firearms, stay for the experience, and if you happen to encounter a large, sarcastic Welsh-American with a distinctly British sense of humor, there's a fairly good chance you've found me.
Seriously, folks. Come check the place out. Good people, good facilities, and a place where responsible firearms ownership and proficiency are taken seriously.
And who knows? I might even manage to teach you something useful.
In the meantime, I'll continue splitting my working life between Enterprise and Center Mass. One job keeps me behind the wheel, the other puts me back on the firing line.
Apparently, retirement isn't something I'm particularly good at practicing for.
Stay safe, shoot straight, and I'll see you on the range.

text:
Andrew, Alexander, and Tanner Skelton disappeared from Morenci, Michigan, the day after Thanksgiving in 2010. The brothers were just 9, 7, and 5 years old, and nearly sixteen years later, no trace of them has ever been found. Their disappearance has been one of Michigan's most troubling unsolved cases, but a major development in the investigation last year has finally brought their father, John Skelton, back before a judge.

The boys had spent Thanksgiving Day with their father and were supposed to return to their mother, Tanya Zuvers, the following day. Instead, they vanished. Skelton was later located at a nearby hospital with an ankle injury, and investigators found his home in disarray. Over the years, he has offered different explanations for what happened, including claims that he entrusted the boys to an underground organization that would keep them safe. Investigators have never found evidence to support that account. In March 2025, a judge granted their mother's request to have all three boys legally declared deceased.

John Skelton was serving a prison sentence for taking the children without permission and was scheduled to be released on November 29th, 2025. Just two weeks before his release, prosecutors charged him with three counts of murder and three counts of tampering with evidence. During seven days of preliminary hearings this summer, prosecutors presented testimony about his movements and statements following the disappearance, including a recorded conversation in which he told his daughter she was now the youngest Skelton. His defense emphasized that the boys have never been located and that investigators have no physical evidence establishing what happened to them.

In September, a judge ruled there was sufficient circumstantial evidence for Skelton to stand trial. His next pretrial hearing is scheduled for December 16th, 2026, although the actual trial date has not yet been set. 

As the sixteenth anniversary of their disappearance approaches, Andrew, Alexander, and Tanner have still never been found. Whatever happens in court, the unanswered question at the center of this case is what happened to those three little boys.

text:
Advertisers Sever Ties With Podcast After Hosts Laugh Uncontrollably at Joke About Digging Up Charlie Kirk

Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan spent nearly 30 seconds giggling on their November 5 episode after reading a post proposing to exhume and kill Charlie Kirk again, triggering an immediate advertiser exodus and a belated Instagram apology once the clip spread.

During the “Drinking MAGA Tears” installment of the “I’ve Had It” podcast, Welch read social-media reactions to Democratic midterm gains, including the line “We’re digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again.” Both hosts lowered their heads and laughed for roughly 20 to 30 seconds before Welch offered “No comment.” Sullivan then asserted that Kirk “was shot by somebody that was super MAGA family,” and Welch agreed he was “shot by a MAGA person.” The exchange was later removed from the YouTube and Spotify versions of the episode.

Cash App responded on X that it does not condone violence of any kind and is no longer a sponsor. Boll & Branch stated it does not currently advertise with the show and will not in the future. Chewy and Lola Blankets confirmed they had ended their affiliations; Zenni Optical paused advertising. The withdrawals followed public pressure that highlighted the hosts’ reaction to the September 2025 assassination of the Turning Point USA founder at Utah Valley University.

Tyler Robinson, charged in the killing, is registered as unaffiliated. His parents are registered Republicans. Family members told investigators he had grown more political in recent years, expressed strong dislike for Kirk, and, according to later reporting, had begun leaning left. Bullet casings recovered with the weapon carried anti-fascist inscriptions. The hosts’ “MAGA person” characterization therefore rests on no public evidence and contradicts the documented trajectory.

The hosts posted a Saturday statement acknowledging that the joke was insensitive, that they should not have laughed, and that nothing is funny about gun violence. The note also reiterated support for “common-sense gun safety reform” and mentioned a donation to Everytown for Gun Safety. The pivot arrived only after commercial consequences materialized.

Market discipline produced a faster corrective than any internal editorial standard. Brands that previously financed a program built on sustained hostility toward conservatives drew a line at open laughter over political murder and corpse desecration. The episode illustrates how certain left-leaning media spaces treat the death of a prominent opponent as entertainment rather than a boundary, and how advertiser exposure can still enforce residual limits on that normalization.

text:
‼️Nick Shirley CAUGHT Lying About Being In New York The Day Charlie  Was ASSASSINATED — And It BLOWS UP Andrew Kolvet's Only Alibi 😱

Nick Shirley was NOT in New York City on September 10th. He was in Utah. A video he posted from the Orem train station that same day catches the ticket agent announcing the location over the PA system in the background — the audio places him minutes from where Charlie Kirk was shot. The next day, September 11th, he films himself at Salt Lake City International Airport, and the scenery outside the window matches public photos of that terminal exactly.

Two clips. Two days. Same state.

That single fact destroys the story he has repeated: that he had already gone back to New York, and that the segment he did with Andrew Kolvet on The Charlie Kirk Show that morning was live. If Nick was standing in Utah on the 10th and again on the 11th, the interview could not have been live. And if it was not live, the one real-time alibi Andrew Kolvet has ever offered for his own movements that morning evaporates.

It gets worse. Nick says Charlie texted him the night of the 9th inviting him onto the show on Thursday the 11th — and that he had originally planned to livestream the UVU event in person before "last-minute obligations" forced him to New York. But Charlie himself was scheduled to be at Charis Bible College in Colorado on the 11th. So why is Charlie trying to book Nick for an interview on a day Charlie already had somewhere else to be? And why does the screenshot Nick released show only a partial thread, cut off exactly where the useful part of the conversation would be?

Then there is the part almost nobody has clocked. In that September 10th train station video, Nick is already pushing the fed-slop line — radical leftists, Antifa, blame the left — before a single fact about the shooter or the motive was public. Not hours later. Not after a briefing. On the day, on camera, before the evidence existed.

Put it together and it stops looking like a coincidence. It looks like Nick Shirley was inserted into the Charlie Kirk timeline to sell the official story to Gen Z before anyone could check it, and to help manufacture an alibi for Andrew Kolvet while he was at it. That is not organic journalism. That is a jacketed asset doing precisely what it was placed there to do.

And here is your update: Nick Shirley says this is all false. So I asked him for the originals of the photos he claims debunk me, so the metadata could be verified. He refused.

He has the files. He has the timestamps. He will not hand them over. You tell me what that means.

Nick Shirley's public answer to all of this is that it's false. Fine. Good. That is exactly what a correction is for — so I went to him privately and asked for the one thing that settles it either way: the original uncompressed files, so the metadata could be checked by someone who actually knows what he's looking at.

Here is what happened.

He opened with confidence: "Yes 100% I filmed it at JFK before I went to the UK." I told him if it checks out, I will apologize and correct the record publicly. He replied, "Yes a correction deserves to be served."

So I asked for the files. Original, uncompressed, straight from the camera roll — WeTransfer, Dropbox, anything, to an email address. Nothing exotic. Just the files.

What came back was a screenshot of the Photos app. A screen recording of a video player. Four photos pasted into the chat. And one file preview captioned "John F. Kennedy International… September 11, 2025 9:39 PM."

Every one of those is a copy of a copy. Re-saved, re-compressed, stripped. A screenshot of a screenshot carries no camera metadata at all. It carries whatever the phone decided to write on the label — which is precisely the thing under dispute. So he has handed me the claim again, not the evidence for it.

And here is where his own defense starts to break. His version is now: "I had an office in NYC that I lived in at that time and was in NYC by Sept 7 and then left for the UK on the 12th." Except there is a clip of him at the Orem train station on the 10th, with the ticket agent calling out the location over the PA. So which is it — New York from the 7th, or Utah on the 10th? Both cannot be true without a same-day cross-country round trip that nobody has produced a boarding pass for.

Look at the airport clip he sent as proof. The label on the file says JFK, 9:39 PM on September 11th. The scenery outside that window is Salt Lake City. He is using a file tagged one airport to prove he was at the other.

He says the timeline is wrong. He has the originals. He will not send them. "A correction deserves to be served" — then serve it.

A screenshot is not metadata. A label is not a timestamp. And a guy who is this confident should not be this hard to get a file out of.
