text:
Live Satsang Transcript with Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar from Gujarat Ashram | 7 November 2026

Source of this transcript 

https://t.co/l4z5cx68Tq

1) Kali, Krishna and Shiva: Different Forms, One Divine Reality

@Gurudev Sri Sri began by discussing the significance of Kali Chaudas and explained the connection between Goddess Kali and Lord Krishna.

He said that Kali and Krishna represent the same Divine principle. The mantra of Krishna and the seed mantra of Kali are also connected. Both represent the destruction of evil and negativity.

Gurudev drew a parallel between the role of Kali in destroying negative forces and Krishna's role in bringing about the destruction of unrighteousness.

He also referred to Krishna's association with Dwarka, which eventually submerged into the ocean, and his identity as Ranchhodrai in Gujarat.

He then explained an interesting connection between Tara, Sita and Rama. Taking 'Ta' from Sita and 'Ra' from Rama gives Tara. Tara signifies the one who helps others cross over. Lord Rama helped so many people cross the ocean of worldly suffering, including Ahalya, Kevat and others.

He also mentioned Goddess Tara's importance in Buddhist traditions and the worship of Lalita Tripura Sundari by Parashurama.

Why do people create divisions between Shiva and Vishnu?

Gurudev questioned the tendency of certain religious groups to insist that Shiva should not be worshipped or even mentioned.

He referred to the Bhagavad Gita, where Krishna says:

"Rudranam Shankaraschāsmi."

Among the Rudras, I am Shankara.

Krishna also says that among the twelve Adityas, he is Ravi, the Sun.

So, Krishna himself acknowledges Shiva as an expression of the Divine.

Gurudev explained that the original intention behind following one particular deity was to keep the mind focused. When someone chooses one Ishta Devata, the mind naturally remains connected to that form of God throughout the day, whether awake, sitting, walking or sleeping.

This intention was not wrong. However, over time, people distorted it and started creating divisions between different forms of worship.

He gave the example of the Ganapati Atharvashirsha, which describes Ganapati as everything, including Indra, Rudra, Brahma, Vishnu and Prajapati.

He then explained how different Puranas glorify different forms of the Divine:

* The Devi Bhagavatam glorifies the Divine Mother.

* The Shiva Purana describes Shiva as the Supreme Reality.

* The Vishnu Purana glorifies Vishnu as the Supreme Reality.

Someone might naturally wonder which one is actually correct.

Gurudev humorously explained:

"Whichever deity's procession is taking place, that deity receives all the praise!"

The point is that every tradition celebrates its chosen form of the Divine as Supreme. There is no need to become confused or create divisions.

This is the beauty of our spiritual traditions.

We always say, "See the One in everyone and see everyone in the One."

Shiva and Krishna are not two separate realities. They are different expressions of the same Divine.

Gurudev concluded this discussion by explaining that Kali is also associated with knowledge, and Krishna imparted the knowledge of the Bhagavad Gita.

The Divine does not merely destroy darkness. It also brings light.

The destruction of ignorance and the awakening of knowledge are two aspects of the same Divine principle.

2. The Psychological Meaning Behind Diwali Crackers

Gurudev asked the audience whether they knew why crackers are burst during Diwali.

He then offered an interesting psychological explanation.

When someone experiences excessive stress, what do they usually say?

"My head is going to burst!"

Almost everyone has used this expression at some point.

Why does this happen?

When we continuously suppress our emotions, frustrations, anger and resentment, they accumulate within us. Eventually, we feel as though something inside us is about to explode.

Gurudev connected this experience with the tradition of bursting crackers during Diwali.

When a cracker bursts with a loud sound, it symbolically represents the release of everything accumulated within us.

The mind experiences a sense of relief:

"Oh! Everything has burst. Now I feel free. Everything is out!"

He also gave the example of people who shout, scream or express their anger intensely. After such an outburst, some people experience a temporary feeling of emptiness and relief.

Gurudev explained that this was the psychological understanding behind the tradition.

In earlier times, throughout the year, people accumulated various negative emotions, including anger, jealousy, resentment and other forms of negativity.

The bursting of crackers symbolically represented releasing these accumulated emotions.

Once you become empty of negativity, you can distribute sweets and share sweetness with others.

The real message of Diwali

Gurudev explained that the real message is to:

* Release the negative emotions accumulated within the mind.

* Let go of anger, resentment and other impurities.

* Light the lamp of knowledge.

* Distribute the sweetness of happiness to everyone.

Simply wishing someone a Happy Diwali isn't enough.

The real celebration happens when we become free from negativity and spread happiness around us.

Let the negativity within you burst, light the lamp of knowledge and distribute the sweets of happiness.

3. Gurudev's Humorous Interaction About English and Gujarati

Gurudev shared an amusing incident involving a Gujarati woman living in America.

She once told him:

"Gurudev, you know, people here in America don't even know English properly. I want to teach them English!"

Gurudev playfully responded that she could certainly teach them, but she would also need a translator!

He then interacted with the Gujarati audience and spoke about the sweetness of the Gujarati language.

He mentioned that he too felt like speaking Gujarati and recalled the old relationship between Gujarat and the Art of Living Bengaluru Ashram.

He explained that when the Bengaluru Ashram was initially established, some of its architectural work and entrance elements had a connection with Gujarat. Sompura artisans from the Baroda region were involved.

He recalled that this was around 1985, when transporting materials and travelling between places was considerably more difficult than it is today.

He also joked about the multiple meanings of Gujarati words and the sweetness of the language.

4. Guided Meditation: Experiencing Coolness Within

Before beginning the meditation, Gurudev asked the audience whether they preferred bhajans or meditation.

Most of the audience voted for meditation, so he invited everyone to sit comfortably.

The following is the sequence of his guided meditation.

*Relaxing the body*

Close your eyes and relax your entire body.

Keep your spine straight.

Take a deep breath and gently exhale.

Gurudev asked everyone to chant Hari Om three times and feel that the sound was reverberating throughout the body, even within the skin and deeper inside.

After chanting, bring your attention to the space between your eyebrows.

Allow the body to become calm and cool.

Moving awareness through the body

Bring your attention to your eyes.

Notice the warmth in your eyes. Gradually move your awareness from your eyelids into your eyes and towards the back of your head.

Don't try to force the warmth to disappear. Allow coolness to develop naturally.

Move your attention behind your head, passing beyond both ears, and then towards the back of your neck.

Gradually bring your awareness to your shoulders and arms.

Imagine that a stream of water is flowing through your arms, carrying your awareness down towards your palms.

Gurudev asked everyone to imagine receiving an abhishekam with milk, as though a gentle stream of milk were flowing over their hands.

Feel the body and mind becoming cool.

Bring your attention to both palms and then to all ten fingers.

Imagine that all the accumulated tension and warmth in your body are flowing out through your fingertips.

Allow the body to become peaceful.

Expanding the mind

Gurudev then asked everyone to allow the mind to expand in all directions.

Just as air spreads everywhere, allow your mind to spread.

The mind is even subtler than air.

Release all expectations, demands and attachments.

Loosen every kind of grip.

There is no hurry. Simply relax.

Allow coolness and peace to spread through your back, abdomen and entire body.

Take a few deep breaths if needed.

Feel the accumulated warmth and restlessness gradually disappearing.

Gurudev explained:

"When the impurities of the mind disappear, the mind begins to expand. When the tension in the body disappears, the body becomes cool."

*Honey abhishekam*

Now bring your attention to the crown of your head.

Gradually allow your awareness to move downwards.

Imagine that you are receiving an abhishekam with honey.

Feel honey flowing over you, gently bathing you and spreading through your body.

Allow this feeling to make you peaceful and sweet.

Move your awareness towards your forehead, eyes and nose.

Observe your breathing.

Notice the warmth in your breath.

Take a deep breath and gently exhale.

Relax your tongue, cheeks and throat.

Imagine sweetness filling your throat.

Gradually move your awareness down towards your chest and navel.

Now release all effort.

Simply relax.

Om Shanti.

Slowly become aware of your body and the surroundings.

Take a deep breath, smile and gently exhale.

Slowly open your eyes.

After the meditation, Gurudev asked the audience how many had experienced a sense of coolness and how many had enjoyed the meditation.

He encouraged everyone to practise meditation regularly.

5. The Deeper Meaning of Panchamrit Abhishekam

After the meditation, Gurudev explained the significance of offering different substances during worship.

He said that when we perform abhishekam to a Shiva Lingam, we should imagine that the Divine is seated within us.

The abhishekam is not merely an external ritual. We should also experience the same qualities within ourselves.

When milk is poured over the Shiva Lingam, imagine that the milk is being poured over you.

Feel your mind becoming cool and peaceful.

Gurudev connected this experience with the concept of entropy.

He explained that when mental agitation decreases, there is greater orderliness within us. As the mind becomes peaceful, our mistakes also reduce.

He then explained the significance of the individual offerings.

*A. Honey: May Everything Become Sweet*

Gurudev referred to the prayer associated with offering honey.

Its intention is that everything around us should become sweet.

May the air become sweet.

May the rivers and oceans become sweet.

May the rays of the Sun become sweet.

May all vegetation become sweet.

May our speech become sweet.

He explained that the word Go has several meanings beyond cows. It can also represent speech, knowledge, movement, attainment and liberation.

Therefore, the prayer is not merely about external sweetness.

May our knowledge become sweet.

May our speech become sweet.

May everything we attain in life become a source of sweetness.

This is the intention behind offering honey.

*B. Milk: May Peace and Prosperity Spread Throughout the World*

Gurudev explained the mantra associated with offering milk:

Apyaayasva sametu te vishvatah soma vrishnyam bhava vaajasya sangathe.

The prayer expresses the wish that everything becomes fulfilled, prosperous, auspicious and beautiful.

He explained the meaning of Apyaayamaan, which conveys the idea of becoming fulfilled, flourishing and growing towards completeness.

The intention is that goodness and prosperity should spread throughout the world.

Gurudev then gave an important example.

Suppose one person possesses enormous wealth. How much can that person personally consume or enjoy?

There is a limit to what one individual can experience.

But imagine if that wealth becomes beneficial to everyone. How much happiness could it create!

This is the real spirit of prosperity.

We should not think only about our own comfort. Whatever wealth and prosperity we possess should become a source of happiness for others as well.

Gurudev compared this with the cool rays of the moon.

Does moonlight cause anger in anyone? Does it trouble anyone?

No. Moonlight spreads a sense of calmness and sweetness.

Similarly, may peace, affection and love spread throughout everyone's life.

When offering milk, have the feeling:

"May the Divine bring this kind of coolness, peace and sweetness into the lives of all beings."

*C. Curd: May Our Vitality and Strength Increase*

Gurudev explained that curd is offered with a prayer for strength, vitality and longevity.

The mantra expresses the wish that our prana and ayush, our vital energy and lifespan, become strong.

May our life force become stable.

May our strength increase.

May our body become energetic and healthy.

He explained that possessing money and everything else is of little use if the body has no strength.

If someone is physically weak and incapable of doing anything, what is the benefit of possessing all the wealth in the world?

The intention behind offering curd is that our vitality and strength should increase.

*The beautiful connection with Krishna and butter*

Gurudev then connected this offering with Krishna's love for butter.

Krishna is famously called Makhan Chor, the butter thief.

Why is Krishna called the butter thief and not the milk thief?

Milk becomes curd, and curd is churned to produce butter.

Gurudev humorously explained that Krishna is waiting for us to undergo this transformation.

First, become like milk.

Then become curd.

Finally, become butter.

And once you become butter, Krishna will come and take you away!

The deeper message is that we must undergo inner transformation.

*D. Ghee: May Our Lives Become Full of Light*

Gurudev explained the mantra associated with offering ghee:

Shukram asi, jyotir asi, tejo asi...

The prayer expresses the wish that our lives become luminous.

May our lives become full of light.

May our brilliance and inner radiance increase.

May our energy, positive qualities and spiritual brilliance grow.

Ghee symbolises illumination and the awakening of positive qualities within us.

*E. Sugar: May Our Very Existence Become Sweet*

Gurudev explained the mantra associated with offering sugar:

Swadu pavasva divyaya janmane, swadur indraya suhavitu namne, swadur mitraya varunaya vayave, brihaspataye madhumān adabhyah.

The prayer expresses a beautiful intention:

May my very existence become sweet for everyone.

May my presence bring happiness to society.

Gurudev humorously explained that it should never happen that people see us and think:

"When will this person disappear? When will this person die? Then society will finally be at peace!"

Instead, our presence should bring happiness.

May our friends experience happiness through us, and may we also experience happiness through them.

May we be pleasant for our friends, society, the Divine and the Guru.

He also explained the reference to Brihaspati, representing knowledge and wisdom.

The prayer expresses the wish that our knowledge and conduct should make us pleasing to everyone.

The real prayer is that our very existence should become a source of sweetness and happiness for others.

*6. Wealth, Relationships and Genuine Good Fortune*

Gurudev returned to the importance of wealth and prosperity.

He explained that whatever wealth, possessions and status we have should become sources of happiness.

If our wealth creates fear, insecurity or suffering, what is the point of possessing it?

Similarly, imagine someone becoming your friend only because of the money in your pocket or your social status.

Would you feel happy about such a friendship?

No.

Having genuine friends, good people around us and positive company is itself a blessing.

Gurudev then shared an example of an 85-year-old woman in America whose son had reportedly taken legal action against her.

He expressed sadness about the situation, particularly because the woman was extremely wealthy, yet her relationship with her son had deteriorated to such an extent.

He emphasised that financial prosperity alone does not guarantee happiness.

Even having children who genuinely love their parents, rather than merely focusing on their wealth, is a blessing.

True prosperity is not simply possessing wealth. It is having the wisdom to ensure that wealth, relationships and everything we possess become sources of happiness for ourselves and others.

*7. The Overall Message of the Satsang*

Throughout the satsang, Gurudev connected devotion, meditation, traditional rituals and everyday life.

His explanations repeatedly returned to a few central principles:

1. Recognise the same Divine in different forms of worship. Do not create divisions between Shiva, Krishna, Kali or other forms of God.

2. Understand the psychological significance of Diwali. Release accumulated negativity, light the lamp of knowledge and spread sweetness.

3. Practise meditation regularly. A calm mind brings clarity, coolness and orderliness.

4. Understand the deeper meaning behind rituals. Every offering represents a prayer and a quality we should cultivate within ourselves.

5. Let prosperity benefit everyone. Wealth becomes meaningful when it spreads happiness beyond oneself.

6. Undergo inner transformation. Just as milk becomes curd and curd becomes butter, allow yourself to evolve spiritually.

7. Make your existence sweet for everyone. Your presence should bring happiness to your family, friends, society and everyone you encounter.

The central message: Spirituality is not limited to rituals and worship. It is about transforming ourselves, becoming peaceful within, recognising the Divine everywhere and making our very existence a source of happiness for others.

text:
In the early 1990s, Jane Seymour was roughly $9 million in debt, raising two young children, and facing the prospect of having no home.

Most people already knew her face. In 1973 she had played Solitaire, the tarot-reading Bond girl in Live and Let Die. 

Through the 1980s she was one of the more sought-after actresses on television. What was less visible was what was happening off-screen. 

In 1981 she married David Flynn. He was not only her husband; he also managed the money. They had two children, Katherine and Sean. 

Jane kept working and kept trusting him with the earnings.
By the early 1990s the money was gone. Investments tied to the housing market had collapsed. 

The marriage ended in 1992. Jane Seymour, a recognizable face on screens around the world, was left with about $9 million in debt and lawsuits from major banks. 

She later described herself in those days as homeless and penniless, with two small children and nowhere left to fall.

She called her agent and said she would do anything. The offer that came back was a risk. CBS had a project about a woman doctor on the 1860s Colorado frontier. 

By the conventional wisdom of the time, the concept looked unpromising: Westerns were out of fashion, shows with children and animals were considered difficult, and family-oriented drama was not seen as a path to success. 

If it became a series she would have to commit for five years, and she had until the next morning to decide. She signed.

Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman premiered on January 1, 1993. The show many expected to fail ran for six seasons and 150 episodes. 

Seymour won a Golden Globe and received two Emmy nominations. For a stretch she was among the highest-paid women on television. 

More importantly, she rebuilt her life, one episode at a time.
The real turning point was not the awards or the ratings. 

It was the night she had every reason to give up and picked up the phone instead. Rock bottom is not always the end of the story. 

Sometimes it is the place where you find out what you are made of. 🌹

text:
THE SAGE

POWER OF PERSPECTIVE

How the Baggage of Our Past Shapes the Landscape of Our Future

“Son,” my mentor, The Sage, reminisced, “many seasons ago, when I was still living in Bridgeport, Connecticut, I had two protégés who appeared to be at the crossroads of life, one cynically and skeptically so; the other proactively and optimistically so. Each one sought my counsel.”

‘I am considering moving to this town. What is it like here, sir?’ The first man asked.
‘What is your current locality like?’ I countered with my own question.
‘It is positively horrid,’ he replied with a heavy sigh, ‘the natives are eminently inhospitable, and they simply do not like strangers in their midst.’
‘You will find this town much the same,’ I replied, ‘I would advise you not to relocate here."

Shortly after his departure, the second fellow arrived and posed the exact same question. Again, I asked about his current location.
‘It is a truly beautiful place,’ he responded warmly, ‘the people are friendly, and I am genuinely happy there. I merely crave a change of environment.’
‘This town is much the same. I think you will like it here.’ I answered him.

“I was to later discover that they both lived in the same town. In fact, they were practically neighbors. The same town. Different opinions of the town. Different responses to their quest. Son, what is your verdict?”

“Sir, the divergence lay entirely in what each person carried internally. Our past experiences tend to tint the lens through which we view the world. When we have been wounded, we default to a morbid state of suspicion. As soon as one experience offers us a dish of disappointment, we start to anticipate the worst in the next experience.”
“Son, doesn’t that end up distorting our perception of reality as it truly is?”
“That is true, sir. In fact, now viewing reality through that faulty prism, we approach new experiences with the baggage of old grievance, unwittingly dragging the ghosts of our past into territories where they have never belonged.”

“Yet, sir, animosity and cruelty do exist, don’t they? Certain toxic situations demand the gift of our absence, don’t they?”
“Absolutely, son! However, learning from the past is one thing; allowing that past to dictate our future is quite another. Relocating to a new town, in the extenuating circumstances, is like altering our external topography without shifting our internal convictions; we merely transplant our old baggage.”

“In other words, sir, we will find ourselves trapped in a vicious cycle, repeating identical patterns of conflict and grievance-collection across different situations and with different people.”
“Absolutely, son! That is why, often, what requires relocation is not our physical body, but our attitude. Additionally, we must critically examine whether we are actually running toward a new possibility; an adventure driven by hope, or merely fleeing a painful memory; an adventure driven by a need to escape. That is why we need true clarity about our real, subterranean intentions. In your cerebral opinion, son, how can we arrive at this clarity?”

I thought long and hard.
“Sir, clarity must come from understanding our motives and asking ourselves two hard questions; ‘Are we willing to cast our net into the pool of infinite possibilities? Or, are we demanding that history repeat itself?’”
“I agree, son. In any case, our past is meant to serve as our teacher, and not sentence us to a lifetime of regret. In the final analysis, it is what we actively seek that will dictate what we notice, even as what we notice shapes how we respond. What is your conclusion on this matter, son?”

“At the end of the day, a genuine fresh start is never found by changing our town; we can embark on a new start only by changing our soul. In other words, sir, we do not need a new world to begin again. All we need is a pair of new eyes. So help us God.”

Yomi Garnett MD

text:
Like a Dragon: Ishin! (2023): Finale Walkthrough

FULL ENDGAME SPOILERS: This part names every remaining story opponent, including the final boss. Stop here if you only wanted help getting to the finale.

14. DAWN BREAKS

Go to Teradaya and agree when Otose offers to call Oryo. Follow the outing's markers: have a meal, choose a marked bar for drinks, then visit Utamaruya for singing. Continue to Nichibuza for the dance portion when the objective directs you there. Finish the outing at Kiyomizu Temple, using the gate at the end of the forest path.

Afterward, visit headquarters and speak to Nagakura, Hijikata and Okita for their individual practice fights.

- Nagakura: watch his heavy rising attacks and thrusts. Evade the full combination before responding.
- Hijikata: his stances resemble Kondo's. Work around his defense or counter after an attack rather than repeatedly striking his guard. When he powers up, be ready to defend against his fireballs.
- Okita: use the timing from your previous encounters. Keep pressure on him when safe, but stop before his counterattack catches you.

These are useful tests of your equipment. If ordinary hits barely make a difference or you burn through medicine, go back into town and improve your setup before departing.

THE POINT OF NO RETURN

The commitment is telling Okita at headquarters that you are ready to leave for Tosa, after the practice fights. The earlier outing with Oryo is not that final cutoff.

Before confirming, make a separate manual save, finish your shopping, check your equipped cards, and fill your usable inventory with recovery items. If you want the Legend completion trophy, change the difficulty before this departure. The final combat stretch does not let you freely change it midway through.

RETURN TO TOSA

Advance with your three allies, defeat the groups in the street, and break the barriers in your path.

BOSS: SASAKI TADASABURO

Remove his supporting soldiers while watching for Sasaki's approach. Your allies give you openings, but don't assume they will draw every attack. When he commits to someone else, strike from behind. His powered sword attacks still deserve space.

Afterward, Nagakura stays behind. Continue through the next enemies and the door into the underground route.

BOSS: ITO KASHITARO

Ito is surrounded by soldiers and fights aggressively. Thin the crowd before concentrating on him. Steam periodically obscures the room, so move toward an edge and use the minimap to avoid being surrounded. Keep your attacks short enough to react when he closes in.

Hijikata stays behind after this fight. Continue with Okita, defeat the group and armored giant ahead, then move along the dock. The offshore bombardment doesn't require you to stop and destroy that vessel. Clear the enemies on your route, complete the button prompt at the end, and board the docked ship.

BOSS: THOMAS GLOVER

Deal with the mounted-gun operators at the rear and the other shooters before settling into the duel. Glover uses two pistols, evasive rolls and kicks to keep you away. Watch his retreat rather than running straight into the shot that follows it.

Close in during his recovery and keep him under pressure when possible. His later fiery barrage can set you alight, so don't ignore a falling health bar while chasing him. Defeat him, then continue alone after Okita stays behind.

Collect the two medicines in the courtyard and heal before entering the castle.

FINAL BOSS: TAKECHI HANPEITA

Be ready for a button prompt as the confrontation begins. The fight changes stages, so don't treat the first depleted bar as the end.

First phase: fight the swordsman patiently. Let him commit, evade or guard, then return a short attack. His ability to withstand hits makes reckless trading expensive.

Second phase: after the next prompt, he combines sword and pistol. Swordsman is useful here because guarding can stop you being trapped in an entire combination. Stay alert for spinning attacks, gunfire and lightning. Use your Trooper abilities when they help rather than saving everything indefinitely.

Final phase: at the top of the tower, he returns to the sword. Expect stronger resistance, including reduced effectiveness from Heat Actions. Keep your health comfortably above danger, defend through his combinations and use the openings. If his summoned blades appear, guarding with Swordsman is safer than trying to rush through them.

Finish the fight and watch the ending. Keep your clear data when prompted so you can continue with Premium Adventure and the remaining side content.

text:
Mary is the restorer of the human race, the redeemer of captives, and the restorer of the ruined world.
.
“Mary not only offered her Son to death in the temple, but was offering him up at every moment of her life; for she revealed to St. Bridget, that this grief which St. Simeon announced to her, never left her heart till she was assumed into heaven. Hence St. Anselm says: Oh Lady, I cannot believe, that with such a sorrow thou wouldst have been able to live one moment, if God himself, who gives life, had not strengthened thee by his divine power. And St. Bernard affirms, speaking of the great sorrow that Mary endured on this day, that henceforth she suffered a living death, bearing a grief more cruel than death. She lived, dying at every moment, because grief for the death of her beloved Jesus, which was more cruel than any death, was at every moment assailing her. The divine mother then, on account of the great merit she acquired in this great sacrifice, which she made to God for the salvation of the world, was justly called by St. Augustine: The restorer of the human race: ‘Reparatrix generis humani.’ By St. Epiphanius: The redeemer of captives: ‘Redemptrix captivorum.’ By St. Ildephonsus: The restorer of the ruined world: ‘Reparatrix perditi orbis.’ By St. Germanus: The consolation of our miseries: ‘Restauratio calamitatum nostrarum.’ By St. Ambrose: The mother of all believers: ‘Mater omnium credentium.’ By St. Augustine: The mother of the living: ‘Mater viventium.’ By St. Andrew of Crete: The mother of life: ‘Mater vitæ.’ For, as St. Arnold Carnotensis says: In the death of Jesus, Mary united her will to that of her Son in such a manner, that both offered the same sacrifice; and therefore the holy abbot says, that thus the Son and the mother effected the human redemption, obtaining salvation for men. Jesus by satisfying for our sins, Mary by obtaining for us that this satisfaction should be applied to us. And hence blessed Denis the Carthusian likewise affirms, that the divine mother may be called the salvation of the world, since by the pain she endured in commiserating her Son (voluntarily sacrificed by her to divine justice), she merited that the merits of the Redeemer should be communicated to men.”
.
(St. Alphonsus Liguori, The Glories of Mary, pp. 467-469)

text:
At 9:53 PM ET, the 82.5 total stayed put.

A total is the combined-score number for a game. Over means the teams need to score more than that number together.

The useful clue here is that the listed number was not the only thing to read. The payout still changed across sportsbooks.

For Oregon State vs Texas State, scheduled for Sat 10:30 PM ET, the Over 82.5 line was 5 minutes old. FanDuel showed +240. Fanatics showed +215.

Translate that into $100. A winning ticket at +240 earns $240 profit. A winning ticket at +215 earns $215.

That $25 difference is easy to miss because both screens still say 82.5. Your wallet does not cash the point number by itself. It cashes the full deal.

The lesson: when a total looks unchanged, check whether the payout quietly moved. That is often where the better or worse offer shows up.

text:
A former FBI special agent is sounding the alarm that the next major attack on the United States may not come through missiles or troops, but through the grocery aisle.
Nicole Parker warns that adversaries only need to hit the systems that keep food cold and available.
Recent refrigeration failures at multiple U.S. military commissaries and supermarket chains in Europe offer a preview of how that could unfold.
In late August, at least six U.S. military bases, including Fort Huachuca (Arizona), F.E. Warren AFB (Wyoming), Naval Station Newport (Rhode Island), Columbus AFB (Mississippi), Travis AFB (California), and Fort Irwin (California), experienced sudden refrigeration failures.
Fort Huachuca reported that “ALL frozen food has spoiled.”
At Fort Irwin, sales were restricted to dry goods.
In at least one case, units were reportedly raised to higher temperatures overnight rather than simply shut off.
The Army Criminal Investigation Division’s Cyber Field Office, Defense Commissary Agency, and Defense Criminal Investigative Service are investigating, along with French authorities.
Officials have not yet confirmed a cyberattack as the cause of the U.S. incidents.
Separately, supermarkets in Sweden, Belgium, and Luxembourg saw refrigeration systems disrupted, with some freezers and coolers reaching 122°F.
Retailers discarded spoiled food.
No ransom demands were made, and those responsible remain unidentified.
Parker, speaking to Fox News Digital, put it bluntly: “Every human being has to eat. This is the grocery store.”
She described these events as asymmetrical warfare, attacks designed to spoil food, empty shelves, and erode public confidence without firing a shot.
“What we’re seeing right now is in Europe and other places, but it can very well happen on our soil,” she said. “No one in law enforcement underestimates the harm that could be caused by a cyberattack against our country or against our allies.”
Her message is clear: law enforcement preparation alone is not enough. Americans should treat this like hurricane season.
Recommended household steps:
• Stock food, water, and necessary medications
• Keep important documents together in one place
• Establish a family communication plan for blackouts or outages
• Have a battery-powered AM radio on hand
“I think if you are prepared, you do not have to fear,” Parker stated. “We’re Americans. We will not falter ever.”
The incidents align with broader recent alerts from the FBI and CISA about malicious actors targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain controllers, systems that protect food and medicine across critical sectors.
Many of these devices remain internet-accessible, unpatched, or still using default passwords.
Preparedness reduces the psychological impact of empty shelves, which can travel faster than any conventional attack.
Food and cold-chain infrastructure now sit at the center of national security concerns.
A coordinated hit on refrigeration systems could spoil weeks of inventory in hours, trigger panic buying, and leave communities scrambling for basic nutrition with little warning.
Enemies understand that hunger and fear move faster than any conventional force, and they are already testing the vulnerabilities.
Household readiness is no longer optional when the systems that keep food safe can be turned against the public itself.
The grocery store is part of the battlefield now.

-Kari Bundy - Health Activist

text:
The country can lose its future without noticing

Let’s establish the premise honestly: there is no established announcement that Elon Musk is being forced out of Texas or leaving the United States. This is a thought experiment about what happens if he—or other consequential builders—decides the next chapter belongs elsewhere.

In Atlas Shrugged, Galt’s Gulch is where productive people withdraw from a society they believe has turned against them.

The real version would unfold through investment decisions.

An expansion built somewhere else. A laboratory opened abroad. A founder deciding that the next company needs more predictable rules than America offers.

The existing buildings remain. Politicians keep pointing at them as proof of national strength.

But the decisions that create tomorrow have moved.

A country can spend years confusing inherited capacity with continued leadership. The children discover the difference when they apply for jobs that were never created.

text:
They consecrated him bishop in secret, inside a monastery the regime had turned into a prison, so their church would not die with them. He never walked free as a bishop.

His name was Tit Liviu Chinezu. Born 22 December 1904 in Transylvania (Iernuțeni, near Reghin, or nearby Huduc, today Maiorești), the son of a Greek Catholic priest, he studied in Rome at the Greek College of Saint Athanasius, took a doctorate in philosophy in 1927, and was ordained there on 31 January 1930.

He taught theology at Blaj and from 1941 to 1945 was rector of its theological academy. In 1946 he was named protopop of Bucharest and worked with students at the Church of Saint Basil the Great. The secret police later listed him among the firmest opponents of absorbing his church into Orthodoxy.

On the night of 28–29 October 1948 he was arrested with the Greek Catholic bishops and other leading priests. Unlike the bishops, first held at Dragoslavele, Chinezu was taken with twenty-five priests to Neamț Monastery. There he refused a demand to abandon Rome. In early 1949 he was moved to Căldărușani Monastery, turned into a prison, where the surviving bishops were held.

The papal nuncio sent word that the Holy Father would be glad if Father Chinezu would accept the sacrifice of the episcopate for the good of souls. On 25 April 1949, Bishop Valeriu Traian Frențiu consecrated him in secret as titular bishop of Regiana, with bishops Iuliu Hossu and Ioan Suciu assisting. He wrote back that he offered his life to serve Peter. He never exercised a public episcopal ministry in freedom.

In late May 1950 the bishops were moved to Sighet prison. Chinezu was never tried. Bishop Iuliu Hossu later wrote that heart disease tormented him, yet he remained calm, gentle, and smiling.

On 4 January 1955, Hossu, Ioan Bălan and Alexandru Rusu were released. They left Chinezu behind, badly ill. Hossu remembered that he smiled, glad to see the first light of their freedom. When the illness worsened, he was moved alone into an isolation cell, with no medical care. He died there on 15 January 1955, aged fifty. Accounts have long said he died of cold; a delayed certificate listed heart and lung disease. Two bishops on sweeper duty that day, Alexandru Todea and Adalbert Boroș, gave him a last absolution. He was buried in the Cemetery of the Poor at Sighet. The grave can no longer be identified.

On 2 June 2019, on the Field of Liberty at Blaj, Pope Francis beatified him with six fellow bishops.

They consecrated him in secret so the church would live. He kept the faith until a cold cell took him. “Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.” (Revelation 2:10)

What would you accept, if it meant the church you love would outlive you?

Sources: Catholic-Hierarchy; Greek Catholic Eparchy of Bucharest biography; Iuliu Hossu, Credința noastră este viața noastră (memoirs); Sighet Memorial; beatification materials of 2019; nuncio Gerald O’Hara’s May 1949 report; Wikimedia Commons.

TO CATHOLICS WHO VOTED FOR PRO-ABORTION DEMOCRATIC CANDIDATES!
Dear fellow Catholics,
We must look a certain issue squarely in the face and be honest with our own consciences.
How can we enter a church, receive the Body of Christ, and profess our love for Jesus Christ—only to then cast our votes for politicians who advocate for abortion—that is, for the taking of the lives of innocent unborn children?
How can we ask God to bless our nation while simultaneously supporting policies that permit the killing of the most vulnerable among us—those who have no ability to defend themselves?
Have we forgotten the teaching of Jesus?
"Love one another as I have loved you."
What, then, of the unborn? Are they not our neighbors? Are they not children of God?
I often hear people offer this justification:
"It’s my body. I have the right to decide."
No! Life is not our absolute property. Your body does not belong to you in the sense that you have total authority to determine life and death—and neither does mine.
We are not the masters of life. We are merely stewards, entrusted by God with the task of protecting it.
Saint Paul reminds us:
"You do not belong to yourselves, for you have been bought at a great price." (1 Corinthians 6:19–20)
We belong to God. Freedom does not grant us the license to act in ways that run counter to His commandments. Having the power to choose does not mean that every choice is morally right.
And one day, each of us will stand before Jesus Christ to give an account for what we have done in our lives.
How will you answer when He asks about the innocent children who never had the chance to see the light of day?
What will you say?
"Lord, I was too busy. I didn't have time to speak up for them. I didn't have time to contact my elected representatives. I voted for them because of other political issues. After all, everyone has the right to choose!"
Do you believe such an answer can justify your conscience before God?
You cannot profess the Catholic faith and claim fidelity to the teachings of Christ while simultaneously disregarding the dignity and the right to life of innocent human beings.
The Catholic Church has consistently taught that direct abortion is a grave moral evil.
The Catechism of the Catholic Church, paragraph 2270, states:
"Human life must be respected and protected absolutely from the moment of conception."
Therefore, Catholics have a responsibility to carefully consider the moral implications when choosing representatives in the political arena.
Supporting a candidate precisely because they advocate for abortion is not a choice that can be easily justified by saying, "It’s just politics."
Let this be clear: The issue here is not simply whether you belong to the Democratic Party or the Republican Party. The question is whether you place your Catholic faith and God’s commandments above your loyalty to a political party.
You cannot prioritize a political party over God’s commandments and then pretend there is no conflict.
You cannot receive the Body of Christ on Sunday morning while turning your back on the innocent lives that God Himself has commanded us to protect.
No one can serve two masters.
Dear fellow Catholics,
It is time for us to wake up and examine our consciences.
Go to confession when you have sinned. Ask God for forgiveness—but do not stop there. Take responsibility for your own choices.
Children are not pawns for politicians to use in their bargaining. Their lives are not something to be discarded at will. An unborn child’s right to life does not depend on whether that child is wanted, whether their existence is convenient for others, or whether they are recognized by the political establishment.
We are not the masters of life; God alone is the Master of life.
And when we stand before Him, no political party, no politician, no position of power, and no justification will be able to take our place or answer for us.
Do not let a political label dictate the conscience of a Catholic.

text:
The Hamster Wheel and the Hungry Ghost

I used to think I was saved, but I wasn't. Everything was still about me. I hope some of you see yourselves in this because God always responds to an honest seeker. 

I lived on a hamster wheel of measuring, justifying, rationalizing, fearing and correcting. I would do something wrong and immediately start calculating. Yes, I did that, but overall I'm a better person than most people. Round and round it went and it never stopped.

That is man under law. That IS the flesh.  It's not you being horny lol. 

I believe the tree of the knowledge of good and evil represents the law. Eating from it changed man's consciousness. It introduced suspicion, fear, shame and accusation. Even a good commandment could no longer be received as good because the mind itself had become divided.

A mixture of light and darkness.

The carnal mind is at enmity with God because it cannot simply receive his love. It must measure everything. It must justify itself. It must know where it stands, and some of you have been given so much talent that I am afraid you might miss this. 

And it is never satisfied.

It is a spiritual vampire.

I finally came to the very painful end of myself and screamed, "Fuck! I can't do this anymore! Save me!"

And the wheel stopped, because I meant it. 

I cannot prove that to anyone. I can only tell you that for almost twenty years the constant measuring in my conscience was gone. God had done something I could never do for myself.

That is the difference between consciousness under law and consciousness in Christ.

In Christ there is only light. Yes, the mind must be renewed, but it is no longer spinning endlessly trying to establish its own righteousness.

It is learning love.

And learning love can be excruciating.

Because once you begin to see people through love instead of law, things you previously accepted become grotesque.

You see the person behind the commandment. You see the woman whose consent didn't matter. You see the suffering that everyone has learned to explain away.

And you begin to hear the hungry ghost speaking out of the mouths of proclaimed Christians.

"But is polygamy actually a sin? God never said so."

"Didn't God put women under men?"

As though the only question worth asking is whether the law permits something.

What about the woman? What about her suffering? What about love?

The hungry ghost doesn't care. It wants to be right. It wants authority. It wants a justification for what it desires.

And I can't hate you for it because I know that ghost. I lived with it for years.

I used to laugh and say all you had to do was collect certificates and degrees and the world would love you.

And it did.

I have books full of them. I look at them now and laugh. They mean nothing.

That was another hamster wheel. Climbing the ladder for status, recognition and God's approval. Always trying to become somebody.

Then God pulled the tablecloth out from under me.

He wasn't subtle.

I lost my health, my jobs, my acceptance into a master's program, my friends. Eventually I couldn't even sit upright.  I literally had to crawl to the bathroom every night and when I was on the toilet I would pass out and wake up with my head on the floor.   Any time my head got above my heart I would go out like a light.  I would literally think of Gollum as I was climbing my way to the bathroom.  

And you know what?

I had the strangest peace.

It was as though God allowed me to experience what it was like to be loved just for who I was.

I couldn't accomplish anything. I couldn't earn anything. I had nothing left to offer.  My own dad tried to talk me into suicide because in his mind if you can't produce you are nothing, but even through that...

I was loved.

I wish all of you could know that kind of love. Not the suffering, but the peace of having absolutely nothing left to prove.

But there was another side to it.

When you're as sick as I was, for as long as I was, and you have a disease where stress can kill you, you learn to dissociate in ways most people can't imagine.

The trouble is that unlearning it is even harder.

After 15 years of being semi-conscious, I probably remember two percent of my life. The rest is gone, until something comes back in a flash. And those memories aren't always pretty.

But I knew I had to remember some things so I prayed for God to enlarge my heart.

Unfortunately, he answered that prayer.

And it's been very hard ever since.

Because what came with feeling again was the ability to see things I had never really allowed myself to see.

I finally faced the actual biblical texts without fear.

And what I saw disturbed me.

Especially what was done to women under the law.

I can no longer call something good simply because it was permitted. I cannot look at a woman being used for reproduction, given into marriage without her consent, or expected to share her husband and tell myself it was loving.

I have tried to override my conscience, but I can't.

Have you looked into the mirror of your own tree of the knowledge of good and evil and seen the reflection staring back?

It is dark. It is insatiably hungry. It will justify almost anything to preserve its own righteousness.

And once you've seen that in yourself, you recognize it everywhere.

The hardest part of faith for me wasn't the agony of dying. It was the void afterward. The space between everything I had lost and a life I somehow had to create from nothing.

People talk about resurrection. They don't talk much about what it's like to wake up in the ruins.

This is why I never minimize another person's suffering.

I don't tell them it's always darkest before the dawn. I don't tell them everything happens for a reason. I don't give them some trite religious platitude so I can feel better about their pain.

No. That will not do.

I listen.

And I don't try to fix.

Some of you will never know that kind of suffering, and I hope you never do. But the least you can do is own the fact that you don't understand it.

You don't have to justify it. You don't have to explain it. You don't have to make it fit your theology.

You can simply love the person in front of you.

The mind under law asks, "Can I justify this?"

The mind in Christ asks, "Is this love?"

And I think that is the difference between the tree of the knowledge of good and evil and the tree of life.

AI Overview
Sako
Surname (Assyrian/Chaldean): Derived as a pet form of the personal name Sargis (the equivalent of Sergius).

AI Overview
These three names share a deep linguistic and historical connection, primarily originating in Ancient Mesopotamia, the Middle East, and the Caucasus.
Sargon
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Greek and biblical translation of the Akkadian regnal name Šarru-kīn. It combines šarru (Akkadian for "king") and kīnu (meaning "true," "established," or "legitimate").
Historical Significance: It is most famously associated with Sargon of Akkad (24th century BCE), the legendary founder of the Akkadian Empire. Later, the Neo-Assyrian ruler Sargon II (8th century BCE) adopted the throne name to establish the legitimacy of his rule.
Sargis
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Classical Syriac and Armenian form of the Latin name Sergius. It originates from the ancient Roman gens (clan) Sergia, which etymologists suspect may connect to the Latin verb servare ("to guard" or "to preserve").
Sako
Origin & Etymology: Sako operates on a few different historical tracks depending on the region:
In the Middle East: Among Assyrians and Armenians, Sako is a popular, affectionate diminutive (or pet form) of the proper name Sargis.
In the Balkans: In Albania, it functions as a standalone occupational surname for a "church servant" or as a nickname for the Muslim name Isak (Isaac).
In Asia: It is also an unrelated Japanese surname (written as 佐古) meaning "HELP" and "ancient".

Sargon of Akkad (/ˈsɑːrɡɒn/; Akkadian: 𒊬𒊒𒄀, romanized: Šarrugi; died c. 2279 BC),[3] also known as Sargon the Great,[4] was the first ruler of the Akkadian Empire, known for his conquests of the Sumerian city-states in the 24th to 23rd centuries BC.[2] He is sometimes identified as the first person in recorded history to rule over an empire.

Birth legend
Sargon is also one of the many suggestions for the identity or inspiration for the biblical Nimrod. Ewing William (1910) suggested Sargon based on his unification of the Babylonians and the Neo-Assyrian birth legend.[75] Yigal Levin (2002) suggested that Nimrod was a recollection of Sargon and his grandson Naram-Sin, with the name "Nimrod" derived from the latter.[76]

LOUIS Raphaël I Sako (Arabic: لويس روفائيل ساكو;[2] born 4 July 1948) is a Chaldean Catholic prelate who served as Patriarch of Baghdad from 2013 to 2026. Pope Francis made him a cardinal in 2018.

Biography
Early life
Sako was born in the city of Zakho, Iraq, on 4 July 1948.[3] He comes from an ethnic Assyrian family of the Chaldean Catholic Church that has roots in a religious community that has had a presence in the city of his birth since the 5th century AD.[4]

He completed his early studies in Mosul and then attended the Dominican-run Saint Jean’s Seminary there. He was ordained a priest on 1 June 1974 and filled his first pastoral assignment at the Cathedral of Mosul until 1979. He then earned a doctorate in Eastern patrology at the Pontifical Oriental Institute. When denied a license to teach because he was only qualified for religious instruction, he earned a second doctorate in history from the Sorbonne in Paris.[5] With this he secured his teaching license and was able to provide religious instruction. From 1997 to 2002 he was rector of the Patriarchal Seminary in Baghdad. He then returned to Mosul and guided the parish of Perpetual HELP for a year.[6][7]

👑🌺🖤 THE ROYAL FAMILY UNITED IN REMEMBRANCE | PART 2 — HONOURING SERVICE, SACRIFICE & THE HEROES WE WILL NEVER FORGET 🇬🇧❤

🌺 A FAMILY’S CONTINUING COMMITMENT TO REMEMBRANCE

For the Royal Family, remembrance is a duty carried across generations.

King Charles, Princess Anne, Prince Edward, Prince William and the other members of the family have longstanding connections with the Armed Forces and the organisations that support military communities.

And it was particularly meaningful to see the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester present tonight.

Only two days earlier, the Duchess of Gloucester had represented Queen Camilla at the Field of Remembrance beside Westminster Abbey, placing a wooden cross among thousands of poppies in honour of the fallen.

From that quiet act of remembrance to tonight’s gathering at the Royal Albert Hall, the message remains the same:

Those who served must never be forgotten.

❤️ FOR THE FAMILIES WHO CARRY THE MEMORIES

Perhaps the most important thing about Remembrance is remembering that sacrifice does not end when a conflict is over.

For some families, it lives on in photographs carefully preserved, letters treasured for decades, birthdays without a loved one and stories passed from one generation to the next.

For veterans, it may live in memories of comrades, friendships forged through extraordinary circumstances and experiences that remain with them throughout their lives.

And for those serving today, it is a reminder that their dedication and the sacrifices made by their families are recognised and appreciated.

Tonight, the Royal Family joined the nation in honouring all of them.

🌺 LEST WE FORGET

As we approach Remembrance Sunday tomorrow, may we remember not only the courage displayed on battlefields, but also the humanity behind every uniform.

The lives lived. The dreams interrupted. The families waiting at home. The comrades who never returned.

To the fallen, we owe remembrance.

To our veterans, we owe gratitude.

To those serving today, we offer our respect.

And to the families who have sacrificed so much, we extend our heartfelt thanks. ❤️

Thank you to the Royal British Legion for another deeply meaningful Festival of Remembrance.

And thank you to the Royal Family for standing together in honour of those whose service and sacrifice must never fade from memory.

Royal Community, tonight I invite you to leave a 🌺 in remembrance of those who served, those who fell and the families who continue to carry their legacy.

We will remember them.

Lest We Forget. 🌺🖤

With love, gratitude and respect,
Whispers of the Crown 👑💙💛

text:
At least half  of the 18 intelligence agencies would have NO intel on nukes in Iran because it isn't their mission to look for it.  Each of the agencies has a specialized mission.

So "all 18 US Intelligence Agencies" NEVER tell a  President the same thing about a specific issue.

Here are some Examples of intel agencies whose missions would not have included looking for nukes in Iran at the time of Trump's decision to attack, and thus would have NO advice or opinion to offer the President about nukes in Iran:

U.S. Army Intelligence (G-2 / INSCOM) supports Army OPERATIONS with intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities.  There was no on-going Army OPERATION in Iran when Trump made the decision to attack.

U.S. Navy Intelligence (N2 / ONI) provides maritime and naval intelligence, including undersea and littoral domain awareness.

U.S. Marine Corps Intelligence: Supports Marine Corps expeditionary and amphibious operations.  No Marine Corps operation was active in Iran when Trump decided to launch the Iran operation.

U.S. Space Force Intelligence (S2). Focuses on space domain awareness, threats to U.S. space assets, and space-based ISR support. Obviously not tasked to look for nukes on the ground in Iran.

FBI Intelligence Branch: Handles domestic intelligence, counterintelligence, counterterrorism, and cyber threats

Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) – Office of National Security Intelligence: Collects and analyzes intelligence related to drug trafficking and its national security implications.

U.S. Coast Guard Intelligence

Department of the Treasury – Office of Intelligence and Analysis (OIA).  Financial intelligence related to terrorist financing, sanctions evasion, and illicit finance.

上周油市按停火来定价，霍尔木兹这两天给出了反例。
布伦特上周五收于98.32美元，全周仍跌约13%，交易员把美伊接触当成供应即将恢复。随后从周六到今天凌晨：美军中央司令部称，在阿曼湾用精确弹药打残圣基茨旗货船Huda的船尾，因其多次无视警告、试图突破对伊朗的海上封锁；伊朗革命卫队海军则称，两艘关闭导航的“违规油轮”分别在海峡以东和海峡内触雷起火，并警告与美军合作、不走指定航道的船只“必将触雷”。这两艘油轮的船旗、船东和独立核实都还没有。
关键不在爆炸本身，而在定价：那13%等于提前兑现了“航运很快恢复”。若保费和通行重新收紧，油价、通胀和12月加息预期会一起动。但现在就写成海峡已经关闭，还为时过早。

Oil spent last week pricing in a ceasefire. Hormuz just offered a rebuttal.
Brent settled Friday at $98.32, still down about 13% on the week, as if U.S.-Iran contacts meant supply would soon normalize. Then, from Saturday into early Sunday: CENTCOM said a U.S. aircraft struck the stern of the St. Kitts-flagged cargo ship M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored repeated warnings and tried to breach the Iran blockade. Iran’s IRGC Navy said two “violating” tankers with navigation systems off hit mines and caught fire—one east of the strait, one inside it—and warned that ships cooperating with U.S. forces on unauthorized routes would “definitely” hit mines. The tankers’ flags, owners and any independent confirmation are still missing.
The point is the pricing, not the blast. That 13% drop prepaid a quick reopening. If insurance and transit tighten again, oil, inflation and December hike odds move together. Calling the strait closed, though, is still a leap.

text:
The American Conservative: The Ukraine Conflict Could Have Been Prevented — Kiev and the West Missed Several Chances for Peace

New details about diplomacy between Russia and the West suggest the war in Ukraine was not inevitable. The publication traces a series of missed opportunities — from the Minsk agreements to the talks in Istanbul.

Minsk was used as a breather. Petro Poroshenko's admission is recalled: the arrangements were "never meant to be implemented." Kiev's goal was to "delay the war — to secure eight years to restore economic growth and build powerful armed forces." The "great diplomatic achievement," as Poroshenko told the Financial Times, was that Ukraine, even "without having an armed forces at all," managed to "keep Russia away from a full-sized war."

Angela Merkel and François Hollande confirmed this: Minsk gave Ukraine the time and space to strengthen its military.

The Istanbul process came close to an agreement. Former MP Vadym Novinsky said that in the first days of the war, on Zelensky's instructions, he organized negotiations. Russia demanded that neutrality and a rejection of NATO be enshrined in the constitution, along with a special status for Crimea and Donbass. Novinsky claims: "I coordinated every point with Zelensky, and at that time he agreed to everything." But the process fell apart — according to him, "our leadership was to blame."

The back channel didn't work either. According to the Financial Times, lawyer Richard Conn and banker Bob Foresman reached Putin through Matthias Warnig. Putin replied that he was "very open to negotiations": a pullback to prewar positions, de facto recognition of Crimea, the return of the ZNPP, and $300 billion for reconstruction. However, according to Warnig, Kiev barely looked at the offer, and Sullivan said Washington had not "approved" the channel.

At key moments, it was Kiev and its Western partners who walked away from diplomacy, not Moscow.

text:
𝐃𝐀𝐍𝐀 𝐖𝐇𝐈𝐓𝐄 𝐎𝐍 𝐓𝐑𝐔𝐌𝐏’𝐒 𝐏𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐒 𝐒𝐄𝐂𝐑𝐄𝐓𝐀𝐑𝐘 𝐎𝐅𝐅𝐄𝐑: “𝐈’𝐌 𝐅𝐋𝐘𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐓𝐎 𝐖𝐀𝐒𝐇𝐈𝐍𝐆𝐓𝐎𝐍 𝐑𝐈𝐆𝐇𝐓 𝐍𝐎𝐖”

The White House press podium has been a revolving door this fall, and on camera Friday, Dana White got asked point—blank whether he’s about to fill it.

“𝘠𝘰𝘶’𝘷𝘦 𝘣𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘰𝘧𝘧𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘫𝘰𝘣 𝘢𝘴 𝘱𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘴 𝘴𝘦𝘤𝘳𝘦𝘵𝘢𝘳𝘺 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘜𝘯𝘪𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘚𝘵𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘴 𝘢𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵. 𝘊𝘢𝘯 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘵𝘦𝘭𝘭 𝘶𝘴 𝘢 𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘵𝘭𝘦 𝘣𝘪𝘵 𝘢𝘣𝘰𝘶𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘺𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘰 𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘱𝘰𝘴𝘵?” a reporter asked the UFC CEO.

“𝘐’𝘮 𝘧𝘭𝘺𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘰 𝘞𝘢𝘴𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨𝘵𝘰𝘯, 𝘋.𝘊. 𝘳𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘯𝘰𝘸.” White said. “𝘚𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘢𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘴!”

Asked how he’d juggle it with his day job running the world’s biggest fight promotion, White didn’t rule it out: “𝘠𝘦𝘢𝘩, 𝘐 𝘨𝘰𝘵 𝘢 𝘭𝘰𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘫𝘰𝘣𝘴 𝘢𝘭𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘥𝘺.” On the specifics of what’s actually been discussed, he kept it close: “𝘐’𝘮 𝘨𝘰𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘰 𝘮𝘦𝘦𝘵 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘩𝘪𝘮. 𝘞𝘦 𝘩𝘢𝘷𝘦 𝘢 𝘮𝘦𝘦𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘰𝘯 𝘔𝘰𝘯𝘥𝘢𝘺, 𝘴𝘰 𝘐’𝘮 𝘴𝘶𝘳𝘦 𝘐’𝘭𝘭 𝘩𝘢𝘷𝘦 𝘮𝘰𝘳𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘬 𝘢𝘣𝘰𝘶𝘵 𝘢𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵.”

It would be a fast turnaround at a podium that’s already churned through two occupants this year. 𝐊𝐚𝐫𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐭𝐭 stepped away in the fall to spend more time with her kids, and her successor, 𝐊𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐞 𝐙𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐚, was out after barely a week on the job. No permanent replacement has been named since.

White has spent years insisting he’s 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚 𝐩𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐬 𝐠𝐮𝐲, even while headlining a UFC card at the White House and standing next to Trump at the podium on election nights. If Monday’s meeting ends with him behind that podium instead of next to it, the fake news is going to wish they’d stayed in the cage.

𝐇𝐞’𝐬 𝐚𝐥𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐲 𝐟𝐥𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐨 𝐃.𝐂. 𝐌𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥.

text:
Donald Trump posted a message on the Truth Social platform publicly offering Dana White the position of White House Press Secretary. During a press conference following a boxing event in London, the UFC boss confirmed that he is flying to Washington immediately and has a meeting scheduled with the President in the Oval Office for Monday (November 9, 2026).

There are several key points to note regarding this proposal:

UFC in the White House: Trump has suggested that White bring prominent UFC fighters—such as Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, and Amanda Nunes—to Washington to serve as his "communications assistants" in the fight against the "radical left."
Broader Personnel Changes: The offer to White coincides with a major shake-up within the Trump administration following the Republican party's defeat in the midterm elections. Concurrently, Stephen Miller has been named the new White House Chief of Staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

Whether Trump’s long-time friend and the architect of the UFC’s rise will trade the fighting arena for the White House briefing room should become clear following Monday’s discussions. Rumors have also surfaced that a boxer might be tapped to replace the Secretary of War. Trump is opening a new chapter in White House politics—a political cabaret, a spectacle tailored for fans of comedy films.   Islam Makhachev, a Russian MMA fighter, current UFC welterweight champion and former lightweight star, is expected to take over as Secretary of War.

🎯 TRUMP OFFERS DANA WHITE WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY ROLE, MONDAY MEETING SET

📍 WASHINGTON, UNITED STATES

🟨 OUR ASSESSMENT: The White House briefing room has already become part of the story before any hiring decision is made. By floating Dana White's name publicly, Trump shifted attention away from a routine staffing vacancy and turned it into a national political spectacle that fits his preference for celebrity-driven politics. White's value to Trump is less about communications experience than his ability to command attention from audiences that do not normally follow Washington press briefings.

If White accepts, daily briefings could become more confrontational and more focused on direct public engagement than traditional message discipline. If he declines, the episode still functions as a test of how far Trump can blur the line between entertainment, sports culture and government appointments. The next challenge is whether the administration wants a press secretary who manages journalists or one who bypasses them altogether.

text:
A senior Emirati official has expressed cautious optimism about US-Iran negotiations, pointing to progress through Qatari mediation while warning that renewed military confrontation remains possible.

Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, chairman of the Defense, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee of the UAE’s Federal National Council, told Fox News Digital that recent diplomatic efforts had offered grounds for hope.

“We see some progress,” he said.

Al Nuaimi said he hoped Washington and Tehran could begin building trust and engage in dialogue that would avert war and produce a political solution. But he cautioned that his optimism did not mean the possibility of conflict could be dismissed.

“We plan for the worst. We hope for the best,” he said, adding that the UAE sought to remain prepared for all challenges and threats.
